definition_zh: 逐步地；越来越；渐进地；累进地
definition_en: in a way that advances by small steps or grows steadily from one stage to the next
core_image: 一级一级抬高的石阶，每级只比前一级高一点点
scene: 山道上的石阶被雨水打得发亮，登山者一步一步往上挪，每走几级就更喘一些。The trail climbed progressively steeper until the ridge flattened out.
sceneCN: 这里指坡度一级一级地变陡（第 1 个义项：随时间或距离一步步向前推进）；句意为山路越来越陡，直到山脊转为平缓。

pos.zh: 逐步地；越来越；渐进地；累进地

derivatives.zh: 逐步的；进步的；渐进派人士
进步主义者；进步主义的

senses.title: Moving forward in small steps
senses.definition: in a way that advances by degrees rather than all at once
senses.definitionCN: 以逐步推进、而非一次完成的方式
senses.example: The fog thinned progressively as the morning went on.
senses.exampleCN: 随着上午过去，雾一点点变薄。
senses.why: The Latin verb progredi means to walk forward, one step at a time; the adverb keeps that measured pace rather than naming a sudden change.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 progredi 意为向前迈步、一步一迈；副词保留了这种有节奏的步调，而不表示突变。

senses.title: Increasing with each stage
senses.definition: used before a comparative to show a steady rise from stage to stage
senses.definitionCN: 用于比较级之前，表示逐级稳定上升
senses.example: The exercises became progressively harder each week.
senses.exampleCN: 每周的练习都变得更难一些。
senses.why: The -ive ending names a tendency that keeps developing, so the adverb can measure one stage against the next and show the gap widening.
senses.whyCN: 形容词后缀表示一种持续发展的倾向，因此副词可以把一个阶段与下一个阶段相比，显出差距逐步拉开。

senses.title: In separate stages of a process
senses.definition: by taking a process one stage after another instead of at once
senses.definitionCN: 把过程拆成一段一段依次进行
senses.example: The course introduces grammar progressively, one structure at a time.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课按部就班地引入语法，一次只讲一个结构。
senses.why: A gradus is a step, so anything done progressively is done step by step, and the stages can be counted and ordered.
senses.whyCN: gradus 就是台阶，因此 progressively 去做的事都是踏阶而行，阶段可以数、可以排顺序。

senses.title: At rising rates on larger amounts
senses.titleCN: 累进地（税率随数额上升）
senses.definition: so that the rate rises as the amount being measured rises
senses.definitionCN: 随着被计量的数额增加，比率也随之提高
senses.example: Higher earners are progressively taxed in most of these systems.
senses.exampleCN: 在多数这类税制中，收入较高者按累进税率纳税。
senses.why: Progressive taxation takes a larger share from a larger base, which is the step-by-step rise of the same root applied to rates.
senses.whyCN: 累进税从更大的基数里取走更大的比例，正是同一个词根所表的逐级上涨用在税率上。

senses.title: Forward along a sequence
senses.definition: moving forward from one item in a series to the next
senses.definitionCN: 从序列中的一项移到下一项
senses.example: The camera moved progressively along the row of portraits.
senses.exampleCN: 镜头沿着那排肖像一张张向前移动。
senses.why: The core motion is walking forward, and in space that motion becomes a sweep along a line of objects.
senses.whyCN: 核心动作是向前走，落到空间里就成了一次沿着排列物件的扫过。

senses.title: Building up without a break
senses.definition: increasing continuously over a period, with no single jump
senses.definitionCN: 在一段时间内连续增长，没有单次跳跃
senses.example: Pressure built progressively inside the sealed tank.
senses.exampleCN: 密封罐内的压力持续不断地升高。
senses.why: If the change happens step after step with no gap, the listener reads it as one continuous build-up rather than a sudden event.
senses.whyCN: 变化一步接一步、中间没有空档，听者就会理解成连续累积，而不是突发事件。

senses.title: Worsening by degrees in illness
senses.definition: used in medicine for a condition that keeps getting worse step by step
senses.definitionCN: 医学用语，指病情逐级持续恶化
senses.example: Her hearing declined progressively over five years.
senses.exampleCN: 五年间她的听力一点点下降。
senses.why: Clinical writing uses the same walking image for a disease that does not stop but takes one more step downward each time.
senses.whyCN: 临床写作把同一个行走意象用在疾病上：它不停下来，而是每次都再向下迈一步。

senses.title: Spreading to more areas
senses.definition: so that the area or group affected grows stage by stage
senses.definitionCN: 受影响的范围或群体逐阶段扩大
senses.example: The policy was applied progressively to every province.
senses.exampleCN: 这项政策逐步推行到每一个省。
senses.why: Forward motion across a map becomes coverage that widens, which is why the word suits phased roll-outs.
senses.whyCN: 在地图上向前推进就成了覆盖面变宽，所以这个词很适合分阶段的推行。

intro.en: Progressively is the adjective progressive plus -ly, and progressive goes back to Latin progredi, to walk forward, built from pro- forward and gradi to step. The direct source is clear; only the first English date of the adverb is approximate.
intro.cn: progressively 是形容词 progressive 加 -ly；progressive 追溯至拉丁语 progredi「向前走」，由 pro-「向前」与 gradi「迈步」构成。直接来源清楚，只有副词在英语中首见的年代是约数。

items.en: Gradus is a step or a stair, and it also gives English grade and gradual, so the whole family starts at a single stair tread.
items.cn: gradus 是脚步、台阶，也给出英语 grade 与 gradual，整个词族都从一级踏步起步。

items.en: Progredi joins pro-, forward, with gradi, to walk, and means to go forward step by step.
items.cn: progredi 把 pro-「向前」与 gradi「走」连起来，意为一步一步向前走。

items.en: The noun progressus, a going forward, supplies the stem that English later borrows as progress.
items.cn: 名词 progressus 意为「向前行进」，提供英语后来借作 progress 的词干。

items.en: English takes progress in the fourteenth century, first as a noun of journeying and then of any advance.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入 progress，先指行程，后指任何进展。

items.en: The adjective progressive appears in the seventeenth century and later names a political camp and a grammatical aspect.
items.cn: 形容词 progressive 于十七世纪出现，后来既指政治派别，也指语法中的进行体。

items.en: Adding -ly gives the adverb, recorded later than the adjective; its exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 加上 -ly 构成副词，记录时间晚于形容词，确切首见年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin step-root gradi and gradus; the second group names slow, step-by-step change without the walking image.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「步」的词根 gradi 与 gradus；第二组指缓慢、逐步的变化，但不带行走的意象。

entries.definition: Advancing step by step, or favouring reform; the adjective behind the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 逐步推进的，或主张改革的；副词所依托的形容词。

entries.definition: The act of moving forward through a series of stages.
entries.definitionCN: 依次经过各阶段向前推进的过程。

entries.definition: Forward movement or improvement; the noun and verb from which the family grows.
entries.definitionCN: 向前推进或改进；整个词族由这个名词与动词生长出来。

entries.definition: Moving backward or returning to an earlier state, built with re- instead of pro-.
entries.definitionCN: 倒退或回到较早状态的，用 re- 而非 pro- 构成。

entries.definition: A series of steps or degrees in a scale, from gradus, a step.
entries.definitionCN: 刻度上的一连串等级，来自 gradus「台阶」。

entries.definition: Slowly, over a period, without sudden changes.
entries.definitionCN: 慢慢地、在一段时间内发生，没有突变。

entries.definition: More and more, used with comparatives to mark a rising degree.
entries.definitionCN: 越来越，与比较级连用表示程度上升。

entries.definition: At a regular, unbroken rate.
entries.definitionCN: 以稳定、不间断的速度。

entries.definition: In small added amounts, one increment at a time.
entries.definitionCN: 以每次一小份增量的方式。

entries.definition: Little by little, through a series of slight changes.
entries.definitionCN: 一点一点地，经过一连串细微变化。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin step-root, the real tax term and the real medical and grammatical uses.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁语「步」词根、真实的累进税术语，以及真实的医学与语法用法。

normal.en: Gradus is a stair tread, so progressively always carries a staircase inside it.
normal.cn: gradus 是一级踏步，所以 progressively 里面永远装着一道楼梯。

normal.en: Progredi is pro- plus gradi: forward plus walk, exactly the picture of walking on.
normal.cn: progredi 是 pro- 加 gradi：向前加走，正是继续往前走的画面。

normal.en: Progressive tax takes a bigger share from a bigger income, step by step.
normal.cn: 累进税从更大的收入里取走更大的比例，正是一级一级上去。

normal.en: Doctors call a disease that keeps worsening progressive, and progress meaning worsening is the same image.
normal.cn: 医生把持续加重的病称作进行性的，这里的「进展」指恶化，用的是同一个意象。

normal.en: The progressive aspect in grammar stretches an action over time, the same way the adverb stretches a change over stages.
normal.cn: 语法里的进行体把一个动作铺展在一段时间上，与副词把变化铺展在各阶段同理。

abstract.en: Progressively is a staircase where nobody can point to the step that changed everything.
abstract.cn: 逐步是这样一道楼梯：没人能指出究竟哪一级改变了全局。

abstract.en: A change that arrives in small steps never gives you a single moment to resist.
abstract.cn: 以碎步到来的变化，从不给你一个可以抵抗的单独时刻。

abstract.en: The last step of a staircase is only high because every earlier step was low.
abstract.cn: 楼梯的最后一级之所以高，只因为前面每一级都还低。

examples.en: The interviews were conducted progressively over three months, region by region.
examples.cn: 访谈在三个月里按地区逐步进行。

examples.en: As the altitude rose, the air grew progressively thinner.
examples.cn: 随着海拔升高，空气逐渐变得稀薄。

examples.en: Standards were tightened progressively rather than in one sudden reform.
examples.cn: 标准是逐步收紧的，而不是靠一次突然的改革。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「普若格瑞西弗利」，里面藏着 progress「向前」：一步一步往前挪，就是逐步地

root: 拉丁语 progredi「向前走」= pro-「向前」+ gradi「迈步」；同族名词 progressus 给出英语 progress，gradus「台阶」另给出 grade 与 gradual。英语由 progress 造出形容词 progressive，再以 -ly 构成副词，副词首见年代为约数，直接来源清楚。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one motion: something moves forward in small measured steps, whether in time, in amount, through stages, along a tax scale, along a row, under rising pressure, through an illness, or across a map.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一个动作：某物以有分寸的小步向前推进——或在时间上，或在数量上，或经过各阶段，或沿税率表，或沿一排物件，或在升高的压力下，或在病程中，或在地域上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flight of stone steps, each one only slightly higher than the last.
core.cn: 核心意象：一段石阶，每一级只比上一级高一点点。

branches.en: THE STEP ITSELF: change that arrives by degrees instead of at once.
branches.cn: 步本身：变化一步一步到来，而不是一次到位。

branches.en: THE RISING LINE: comparison that widens stage by stage, and pressure that builds without a break.
branches.cn: 上升的线：逐级拉开的比较，以及不间断累积的压力。

branches.en: THE ORDER: a process taken stage by stage, and a sweep along a series of objects.
branches.cn: 顺序：把过程分阶段来做，以及沿一串物件的扫过。

branches.en: THE SCALE OF RATES: a tax that takes a larger share from a larger base.
branches.cn: 比率的刻度：基数越大、取走比例越高的税。

branches.en: THE WIDENING COURSE: a disease that keeps descending, and a policy that reaches more places.
branches.cn: 扩大的进程：不断下行的病情，以及覆盖更多地方的政策。

intro.en: Progressively is English -ly added to progressive, which is Latin progressus plus -ive. The Latin line runs from gradi, to step, through progredi, to walk forward.
intro.cn: progressively 是英语后缀 -ly 加在 progressive 上，而 progressive 是拉丁语 progressus 加 -ive。拉丁语这条线从 gradi「迈步」经 progredi「向前走」延伸而来。

latinIntro.en: Gradus, gradi and progressus belong to one walking family; pro- marks direction only and adds no new root.
latinIntro.cn: gradus、gradi 与 progressus 同属一个「行走」词族；前缀 pro- 只标方向，不带来新词根。

items.example: Every sense of the English word still contains this single stair tread.
items.exampleCN: 这个英语词的每个义项里都还装着这一级台阶。

items.example: The verb supplies the act of stepping that -ive turns into a tendency.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供迈步的动作，后缀 -ive 再把它转为一种倾向。

items.example: Forward plus walk is the whole picture behind the adverb.
items.exampleCN: 「向前」加「走」就是副词背后的整个画面。

items.example: English borrows the noun as progress.
items.exampleCN: 英语把这个名词借作 progress。

items.example: It marks direction and contrasts with re- in regressive.
items.exampleCN: 它标出方向，并与 regressive 中的 re- 相对。

items.example: The suffix turns the act of advancing into an ongoing tendency.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「向前推进」的动作变成一种持续倾向。

items.example: The adjective is the base the adverb is built on.
items.exampleCN: 形容词是副词的构词基础。

items.example: The suffix -ly turns the adjective into a modifier of manner.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 把形容词变成方式状语。

items.example: The noun names the whole staircase rather than one step.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指整道楼梯，而不是某一级。

items.example: It is the last link between the Latin stem and English usage.
items.exampleCN: 它是拉丁词干与英语用法之间的最后一环。

latinEntries.structure: progredi (v., compound of pro- and gradi)

definition_zh: 主要地；占主导地位地；绝大多数地
definition_en: mainly, or in a way that holds the largest share or the strongest influence
core_image: 一片林子里九成是同一种树，其余只在林缘零星几棵
scene: 集市上几十个摊位卖的全是同一种粗布，只有两个摊子摆着别的东西。The market is predominantly a cloth market, with only two stalls selling anything else.
sceneCN: 这里指集市在整体上以布市为主（第 1 个义项：大部分情况下、主要地）；句意为这个集市主要是布市，只有两个摊子卖别的东西。

pos.zh: 主要地；占主导地位地；绝大多数地

derivatives.zh: 支配的；显性的；显性性状

senses.title: For the most part
senses.definition: mainly, when describing what something is mostly like
senses.definitionCN: 描述某事物大体属何种情况时的「主要地」
senses.example: The region is predominantly agricultural.
senses.exampleCN: 这个地区以农业为主。
senses.why: Prae- means in front or before, and dominari means to rule, so what is predominant rules the description from the front of the line.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语前缀表示「在前」，词根意为「统治」，因此占据主导者是从队列最前面统摄整体描述的那一项。

senses.title: Holding the majority in number
senses.definition: making up more than half of a countable group
senses.definitionCN: 在一个可数的群体中占一半以上
senses.example: The audience was predominantly female.
senses.exampleCN: 观众以女性为主。
senses.why: Counting is the plainest form of ruling: the larger part outnumbers the rest and therefore sets the tone of the whole.
senses.whyCN: 数数是「统治」最朴素的形式：较大的那部分在人数上压过其余，因而定下整体的调子。

senses.title: Dominating by influence
senses.definition: so that the strongest group or factor controls decisions
senses.definitionCN: 最强的一方或因素控制着决定
senses.example: Decision-making is predominantly in the hands of a few officials.
senses.exampleCN: 决策权主要掌握在少数官员手中。
senses.why: Here power, not number, is what rules; the adverb measures who actually decides rather than who is present.
senses.whyCN: 这里统摄局面的是权力而非人数；副词衡量的是谁真正决定，而不是谁在场。

senses.title: Forming the main ingredient
senses.definition: making up the largest part of a mixture or material
senses.definitionCN: 在混合物或材料中占最大份额
senses.example: The rock is predominantly quartz.
senses.exampleCN: 这块岩石的主要成分是石英。
senses.why: Mineralogy borrows the word for the mineral that holds the largest share of the mass, where ruling means occupying most of the substance.
senses.whyCN: 矿物学借这个词指占质量份额最大的矿物，这里的「统治」指占据物质的大半。

senses.title: Typically of one kind
senses.definition: in most cases of a stated kind, as a general pattern
senses.definitionCN: 在多数情况下属于所述类型，构成一般规律
senses.example: Winters here are predominantly dry.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的冬天多为干燥天气。
senses.why: A prevailing pattern is a ruler in time: it holds sway over most seasons without forbidding exceptions.
senses.whyCN: 气候上的主导型态是时间里的统治者：它在多数季节掌权，但不必排除例外。

senses.title: Prevailing in colour or style
senses.definition: appearing as the main colour or visual character
senses.definitionCN: 作为主要颜色或视觉特征出现
senses.example: The walls were predominantly white, with dark wooden beams.
senses.exampleCN: 墙面以白色为主，配深色木梁。
senses.why: The eye reads a large field as the ground of a picture, so the colour that fills it is literally predominant in the scene.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛把大片区域读作画面的底子，因此填满这片区域的颜色在视觉上确实「占据前景之外的全体」。

senses.title: In ancestry or composition
senses.titleCN: 以某种族群或来源为主
senses.definition: so that most members of a population come from one stated origin
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体中多数成员来自所述来源
senses.example: The city's population is predominantly of rural origin.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市的人口以农村出身者为主。
senses.why: Demography counts origins, and the largest origin group sets the profile of the population as a whole.
senses.whyCN: 人口学统计来源，最大的来源群体为整体人口定下轮廓。

senses.title: Above all, when ranking causes
senses.definition: as the main reason among several that could be named
senses.definitionCN: 在可以列出的多个原因中作为主要原因
senses.example: The failure was predominantly a matter of poor planning.
senses.exampleCN: 这次失败首要的是规划不当。
senses.why: Among competing explanations the dominant one carries the argument, so the adverb ranks causes rather than describing a crowd.
senses.whyCN: 在相互竞争的解释里，主导的那一个承担了论证，因此副词是在给原因排序，而不是描述人群。

intro.en: Predominantly is predominant plus -ly, and predominant is Latin prae-, in front, with dominari, to rule, from dominus, master. The medieval Latin form praedominari is recorded; the direct source is clear and only the English date is approximate.
intro.cn: predominantly 是 predominant 加 -ly；predominant 来自拉丁语 prae-「在前」加 dominari「统治」，后者出自 dominus「主人」。中古拉丁语有 praedominari 这一形式；直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: Dominus is the master of a household, and it also gives English dominate and dominion.
items.cn: dominus 是一户之主，也给出英语 dominate 与 dominion。

items.en: The verb dominari means to be master, to rule, and it is the source of the ruling image in the whole family.
items.cn: 动词 dominari 意为做主、统治，是整个词族中「统治」意象的来源。

items.en: Prae- means before or in front; joined to dominari it yields the sense of ruling over others, standing first.
items.cn: prae- 意为在前、在旁；与 dominari 相连即得「凌驾于他人之上、站在最前」之义。

items.en: Scholastic and legal Latin use praedominari for holding the upper hand, and the participle passes into French and English.
items.cn: 经院与法律拉丁语用 praedominari 表示占上风，其分词形式传入法语与英语。

items.en: Predominant enters English in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, first in theology and then in general description.
items.cn: predominant 于十六、十七世纪进入英语，先用于神学，后用于一般描述。

items.en: The adverb predominantly is a later formation; its exact first date is uncertain, and it spreads with statistics and survey writing.
items.cn: 副词 predominantly 是较晚的构词，确切首见年代不确定，随统计与调查报告的写作而普及。

note.en: The first group shares the dominus ruling-root; the second group names majority without the image of a master.
note.cn: 第一组共享 dominus「主人」这一统治词根；第二组表示多数，但不带「主人」的意象。

entries.definition: Holding the largest share or the strongest position; the adjective behind the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 占最大份额或最强地位的；副词所依托的形容词。

entries.definition: To be the strongest or most numerous element.
entries.definitionCN: 成为最强或数量最多的成分。

entries.definition: The state of holding the upper hand.
entries.definitionCN: 占上风的状态。

entries.definition: Ruling or most conspicuous, built on dominus without the prae- prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 支配的、最显眼的，只用 dominus、不带 prae- 前缀。

entries.definition: To control or tower over others.
entries.definitionCN: 控制他人或高踞其上。

entries.definition: For the greater part; more than anything else.
entries.definitionCN: 大部分；最主要地。

entries.definition: Above all other things, often ranking importance.
entries.definitionCN: 首要地，常用于排重要性。

entries.definition: To a great extent, with room left for exceptions.
entries.definitionCN: 在很大程度上，留有例外余地。

entries.definition: In most cases or for most of the time.
entries.definitionCN: 在多数情况下或多数时间里。

entries.definition: First in rank or purpose, rather than in number.
entries.definitionCN: 在等级或目的上居首，而非数量上占多。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real dominus root, the real prae- prefix and the real survey phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的 dominus 词根、真实的 prae- 前缀与真实的调查用语。

normal.en: Dominus is the master of the house, so predominant means the one that runs the place.
normal.cn: dominus 是一屋之主，所以 predominant 就是「管着这个地方」的那一个。

normal.en: Prae- puts the ruler in front, which is why the word also means standing first in a ranking.
normal.cn: prae- 把统治者放在最前，所以这个词也指在排序中居首。

normal.en: Survey reports love the phrase predominantly rural, because counting is the easiest way to be dominant.
normal.cn: 调查报告爱用「以乡村为主」这类说法，因为数数是最容易显出的主导。

normal.en: Predominantly white walls are not all white; the word always leaves room for the dark beams.
normal.cn: 「以白色为主」的墙面并非全白；这个词总给深色木梁留了位置。

normal.en: Predominant does not mean total: it means first among others, not alone.
normal.cn: predominant 不等于全部：它指在众者之中居首，而不是唯一。

abstract.en: What predominates sets the temperature of the room, even when it is not every person in it.
abstract.cn: 占主导者决定房间的温度，即便它不是屋里的每一个人。

abstract.en: Majority is a claim about weight, and weighting is how a crowd becomes a direction.
abstract.cn: 多数是关于分量的判断，而分量正是人群变成方向的方式。

abstract.en: The predominant colour is the one the eye stops noticing.
abstract.cn: 占主导的颜色，恰恰是眼睛不再注意的那一种。

examples.en: The workforce is predominantly young and predominantly urban.
examples.cn: 劳动力以年轻人为主，也以城市人口为主。

examples.en: Its exports are predominantly raw materials rather than finished goods.
examples.cn: 它的出口以原材料为主，而非成品。

examples.en: The debate was predominantly about cost, not about safety.
examples.cn: 这场争论主要围绕成本，而不是安全。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「普瑞多米南特利」，domi 让人想到「家庭」里做主的人：一家人里做主的那位，就是占主导地

root: 拉丁语 prae-「在前」+ dominari「统治」（出自 dominus「主人」）→ 中古拉丁语 praedominari「占上风」→ 英语 predominant，再加 -ly 成副词。直接来源清楚；英语首见年代为约数。同族 dominant、dominate、dominance 均出自 dominus，但都不带 prae- 前缀。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all ask which side is bigger or stronger: the general character, the head count, the hand on the decision, the main ingredient, the usual weather, the colour that fills the field, the largest ancestry group, and the leading cause.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在问「哪一边更大或更强」：整体性质、人数、决策之手、主要成分、常见天气、填满画面的颜色、最大的来源群体，以及首要原因。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a forest where nine trees in ten are the same species.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片林子，十棵树里有九棵是同一树种。

branches.en: THE GENERAL CHARACTER: what something is mostly like, stated in one word.
branches.cn: 整体性质：用一句话说出某物大体是什么样子。

branches.en: THE COUNT: more than half of a group, measured by heads.
branches.cn: 计数：按人头算，超过群体的一半。

branches.en: THE HAND ON THE DECISION: influence rather than number holding the upper hand.
branches.cn: 决策之手：占上风的是影响力而非人数。

branches.en: THE BULK: the mineral that fills most of the rock, and the origin group that fills most of the population.
branches.cn: 主体：填满岩石大半的矿物，以及构成人口大半的来源群体。

branches.en: THE SETTING TONE: the usual weather, the colour that fills the wall, and the leading explanation.
branches.cn: 定调者：常见的天气、填满墙面的颜色，以及首要的解释。

intro.en: Predominantly is -ly on predominant, which is prae- plus dominari plus -ant. The Latin line is dominus, master, then dominari, to rule.
intro.cn: predominantly 是 -ly 加在 predominant 上，而 predominant 是 prae- 加 dominari 再加 -ant。拉丁语这条线是 dominus「主人」，再到 dominari「统治」。

latinIntro.en: Dominus and dominari carry the ruling sense; prae- adds position in front, and -ant and -ly only change the part of speech.
latinIntro.cn: dominus 与 dominari 承载「统治」义；prae- 加上「在前」的位置，-ant 与 -ly 只改变词性。

items.example: The noun supplies the figure of the one who rules.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供「统治的那一位」这一形象。

items.example: The verb turns the master into the act of ruling.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把「主人」变成统治的行为。

items.example: The prefix places the ruling element at the head of the line.
items.exampleCN: 前缀把统治的那一项放在队列最前。

items.example: It turns the verb into an adjective of state.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词变成表状态的形容词。

items.example: The shorter form marks the strongest element without the prefix.
items.exampleCN: 不带前缀的短形式标出最强的那一项。

items.example: The verb keeps the plain ruling sense of dominari.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词保留 dominari 平实的统治义。

items.example: The compound adds the idea of standing first among rivals.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合形式加上「在对手中居首」的意思。

items.example: The verb is the action behind the adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是副词背后的动作。

items.example: The adverb lets the writer describe a whole in one word.
items.exampleCN: 副词让作者用一个词描述整体。

items.example: The noun names the state, not the manner.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指状态，而非方式。

definition_zh: 相对地；比较而言；按比例地
definition_en: when judged in comparison with something else, rather than on an absolute scale
core_image: 两把尺子并排放着，一把长一把短，长短只在比较中才成立
scene: 河面结了一层薄冰，孩子们试探着踩上去，冰面发出细碎的响声，却没有裂开。The ice held, relatively thin but strong enough for the children.
sceneCN: 这里指冰层相对来说很薄（第 2 个义项：程度上「还算」，用于弱化形容词）；句意为冰面虽然相对薄，却结实得足以承受孩子们。

pos.zh: 相对地；比较而言；按比例地

derivatives.zh: 相对主义者；相对主义的

senses.title: Judged against something else
senses.titleCN: 与别的东西比较之后判断
senses.definition: when measured in comparison with another case rather than on its own
senses.definitionCN: 与另一情形比较之后衡量，而非单独衡量
senses.example: The exam was relatively easy this year.
senses.exampleCN: 今年的考试相对容易。
senses.why: Relativus in Latin means having reference to something; the adverb always points to a second term that the sentence may leave unspoken.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 relativus 意为「有所参照的」；这个副词永远指向另一个比较项，而那个项可以不出现在句子里。

senses.title: To a moderate degree
senses.definition: fairly or somewhat, when softening a strong adjective
senses.definitionCN: 修饰语气较强的形容词时，表示「还算、比较」
senses.example: The hotel is relatively cheap for this district.
senses.exampleCN: 对这一带来说，这家旅馆算便宜。
senses.why: By tying the adjective to a comparison, the speaker avoids claiming it outright, which is why relatively works as a hedge.
senses.whyCN: 把形容词拴在比较上，说话人就不必把话说满，这正是 relatively 能起缓和作用的原因。

senses.title: In proportion to the whole
senses.definition: so that the size of one thing is weighed against the size of another
senses.definitionCN: 把一物的大小放在另一物的大小上衡量
senses.example: The cost is relatively small next to the size of the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 相对于预算规模，这笔花费比较小。
senses.why: Proportion is the literal content of reference: the word reports a ratio, not a bare quantity.
senses.whyCN: 比例正是「参照」的字面内容：这个词报告的是一个比值，而不是一个光秃秃的数量。

senses.title: Not absolute: motion and frame
senses.titleCN: 非绝对（物理上相对于参照系）
senses.definition: in physics, so that a quantity is defined only against a chosen frame
senses.definitionCN: 物理上指某量只有相对于选定参照系才有定义
senses.example: Speed is always relatively defined, never on its own.
senses.exampleCN: 速度总是相对地被定义，从不单独成立。
senses.why: Physics made this the technical sense: relativity says no frame is privileged, so every measurement is a comparison.
senses.whyCN: 物理学把它用成术语：相对论认为没有哪个参照系更优越，因此每次测量都是一次比较。

senses.title: Compared with its own kind
senses.definition: when set beside other members of the same class
senses.definitionCN: 放在同类其他成员旁边衡量
senses.example: The species is relatively rare in the north.
senses.exampleCN: 这个物种在北方相对少见。
senses.why: The comparison hides inside the noun phrase: rare compared with other species, not rare in the absolute.
senses.whyCN: 比较藏在名词短语里：是与其他物种比而少见，不是在绝对意义上少见。

senses.title: Against a statistical average
senses.titleCN: 以平均值或中位数为基准
senses.definition: when measured against the median or average of a whole population
senses.definitionCN: 以一个整体的中位数或平均数作为基准衡量
senses.example: Wages here are relatively high against the national average.
senses.exampleCN: 与全国平均相比，这里的工资相对较高。
senses.why: Statistics needs a baseline, and the adverb turns the baseline into the hidden second half of the sentence.
senses.whyCN: 统计需要一个基准，而副词把这个基准变成句子中隐藏的另一半。

senses.title: By interval in music
senses.definition: in music, by the distance between notes rather than by fixed pitch
senses.definitionCN: 音乐上按音与音之间的距离，而不按固定音高
senses.example: Children learn pitch relatively, by tracking intervals rather than fixed notes.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子学音高是相对地学，靠跟踪音程而不是记住固定音。
senses.why: Relative pitch is the ear's ability to place a note by its distance from another, which is the same reference structure applied to sound.
senses.whyCN: 相对音高是耳朵靠一个音到另一个音的距离来定位音的能力，正是同一参照结构用在声音上。

senses.title: In the fixed phrase relatively speaking
senses.definition: in the set phrase relatively speaking, marking the whole statement as qualified
senses.definitionCN: 在「相对而言」这一固定说法中，把整句标记为有保留
senses.example: Relatively speaking, the second trial was a failure.
senses.exampleCN: 相对而言，第二次试验算是失败。
senses.why: The phrase turns the adverb into a frame for the clause, warning that the verdict depends on the comparison chosen.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把副词变成整句的框架，提醒结论取决于所选的比较对象。

intro.en: Relatively is relative plus -ly, and relative comes from Latin relativus, from referre, to carry back, built from re- back and ferre to carry. The direct source is clear; only the first English date is approximate.
intro.cn: relatively 是 relative 加 -ly；relative 出自拉丁语 relativus，来自 referre「带回」，由 re-「回」与 ferre「携带」构成。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: Ferre means to carry, and it also lies behind transfer, refer and offer.
items.cn: ferre 意为携带，也藏在 transfer、refer 与 offer 背后。

items.en: Re- plus ferre gives referre, to carry back, hence to bring into relation with something.
items.cn: re- 加 ferre 得 referre「带回」，引申为把某物与另一物联系起来。

items.en: Late Latin relativus means having reference to something else, a grammatical and philosophical term before an everyday one.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 relativus 意为「与他物有参照关系的」，先是语法与哲学术语，后来才进入日常语。

items.en: English takes relative in the fourteenth century for grammar and kinship, and later for comparison in general.
items.cn: 英语于十四世纪借入 relative，用于语法与亲属关系，后来泛指比较。

items.en: Nineteenth and twentieth century physics fixes the word in relativity, where every measurement is a comparison.
items.cn: 十九、二十世纪的物理学把这个词固定在「相对性」上，其中一切测量都是比较。

items.en: The adverb relatively spreads with scientific and statistical writing; its exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 副词 relatively 随科学与统计写作普及，确切首见年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the ferre carrying-root and its re- prefix; the second group names comparison and hedging without the reference image.
note.cn: 第一组共享 ferre「携带」词根及 re- 前缀；第二组表示比较与保留语气，但不带参照的意象。

entries.definition: Defined by reference to something else; also a family member.
entries.definitionCN: 需参照他物才有定义的；也指亲属。

entries.definition: The principle that measurements depend on the frame of reference.
entries.definitionCN: 测量取决于参照系的原则。

entries.definition: A connection between two things, from the same referre stem.
entries.definitionCN: 两物之间的关联，出自同一个 referre 词干。

entries.definition: To connect or to tell, built on the same reference idea.
entries.definitionCN: 联系或讲述，建立在同一个参照概念上。

entries.definition: Statistically linked, built with co- rather than re- and not a form of relative.
entries.definitionCN: 统计上相关的，用 co- 而非 re- 构成，不是 relative 的变形。

entries.definition: When compared with others of the same kind.
entries.definitionCN: 与同类其他者比较时。

entries.definition: To a moderate degree, softening the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 程度上中等，起缓和形容词的作用。

entries.definition: Slightly; to a limited degree.
entries.definitionCN: 稍微；到有限的程度。

entries.definition: To a noticeable degree, often before a stronger word than expected.
entries.definitionCN: 到明显程度，常用于比预期更强的词前。

entries.definition: At a size or rate that matches the whole.
entries.definitionCN: 与整体相称的大小或比例。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real referre root, the real physics term and the real statistical baseline.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的 referre 词根、真实的物理术语与真实的统计基准。

normal.en: Ferre is to carry, so relative means carried back to something else for comparison.
normal.cn: ferre 是携带，所以 relative 意为「被带回去对照另一物」。

normal.en: Referre gives refer, and referring is exactly what relatively does: it points at an unspoken second term.
normal.cn: referre 给出 refer，而「指涉」正是 relatively 做的事：它指向一个没说出口的比较项。

normal.en: In physics every speed is relative, because there is no privileged frame to measure against.
normal.cn: 物理上一切速度都是相对的，因为没有哪个参照系享有特权。

normal.en: Relative pitch is placing a note by its distance from another note, not by its fixed height.
normal.cn: 相对音高是按一个音到另一个音的距离定位，而不是按它的固定高度。

normal.en: Relatively speaking is a warning label: the verdict holds only against the baseline we chose.
normal.cn: 「相对而言」是一张警示标签：结论只在对我们所选的基准成立。

abstract.en: A ruler measures nothing until you decide what it is laid against.
abstract.cn: 尺子在你决定拿它比什么之前，什么也量不出。

abstract.en: Relative is the admission that no number stands alone in the room.
abstract.cn: 相对，是承认没有哪个数字能独自站在房间里。

abstract.en: The word quietly adds a second sentence that the speaker never says aloud.
abstract.cn: 这个词悄悄补上了说话人从不明说的第二句话。

examples.en: The sample is relatively small, so the conclusion stays provisional.
examples.cn: 样本相对较小，因此结论仍是暂时的。

examples.en: Prices here are relatively low, relatively speaking, for a capital city.
examples.cn: 相对而言，作为首都，这里的物价还算低。

examples.en: The reaction is relatively slow at room temperature.
examples.cn: 在室温下这个反应相对缓慢。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「瑞雷提弗利」，relate 是「联系」：凡事一联系、一比较，就成了相对地

root: 拉丁语 referre「带回、参照」= re-「回」+ ferre「携带」→ 晚期拉丁语 relativus「有参照关系的」→ 英语 relative，再加 -ly 成副词。直接来源清楚；英语首见年代为约数。同族 relation、relate、relativity 同出 referre；correlate 用 co- 前缀，另成一支。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all hide a second term: a comparison partner, a softened adjective, a ratio to the whole, a frame of reference, the rest of its class, a statistical baseline, the interval between notes, and the fixed phrase that flags the whole claim.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都藏着一个第二项：比较对象、被缓和的形容词、与整体的比例、参照系、同类其他成员、统计基准、音与音的音程，以及为整句加保留的固定说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two rulers laid side by side, long and short only because of each other.
core.cn: 核心意象：两把并排放着的尺子，长与短只因彼此而成。

branches.en: THE HIDDEN COMPARISON: judged against a case the sentence need not name.
branches.cn: 隐藏的比较：对着一个句子不必点名的情形衡量。

branches.en: THE SOFTENED WORD: a strong adjective pulled back to a moderate degree.
branches.cn: 被缓和的词：把强形容词拉回到中等程度。

branches.en: THE BASELINE: a ratio to the whole, and a figure set against a national average.
branches.cn: 基准：与整体的比例，以及对着全国平均数看的数字。

branches.en: THE FRAME: motion defined only against a chosen frame, and pitch placed by interval.
branches.cn: 参照系：运动只在选定参照系下才有定义，音高则按音程定位。

branches.en: THE PEER AND THE PHRASE: rare beside its own kind, and the fixed warning relatively speaking.
branches.cn: 同类与套语：在同类中显得少见，以及「相对而言」这句固定提醒。

intro.en: Relatively is -ly on relative, and relative is Latin relativus, from referre, to carry back. The reference idea lives in the prefix re- plus the verb ferre.
intro.cn: relatively 是 -ly 加在 relative 上，而 relative 是拉丁语 relativus，出自 referre「带回」。参照义就住在前缀 re- 与动词 ferre 里。

latinIntro.en: Ferre is the carrying verb behind transfer and refer; re- sends the carrying back, which produces the idea of reference.
latinIntro.cn: ferre 是藏在 transfer 与 refer 背后的「携带」动词；re- 让携带折返，于是产生「参照」的概念。

items.example: The verb supplies the carrying that comparison performs.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供比较所执行的那次携带。

items.example: It turns carrying into carrying back, and so into reference.
items.exampleCN: 它把「携带」变成「带回来」，于是成为参照。

items.example: English refer and reference come straight from this verb.
items.exampleCN: 英语的 refer 与 reference 直接出自这个动词。

items.example: The adjective is a grammar term before it becomes everyday.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词先是语法术语，后来才成为日常用词。

items.example: English extends the term from grammar to kinship and to comparison.
items.exampleCN: 英语把这个词从语法扩展到亲属关系与比较。

items.example: The adverb turns the reference into a way of measuring.
items.exampleCN: 副词把「参照」变成一种衡量的方式。

items.example: The noun names the link that comparison assumes.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指比较所预设的那条联系。

items.example: Physics makes the reference idea into a law.
items.exampleCN: 物理学把这个参照概念做成了一条定律。

items.example: The verb is the plain action of putting two things in relation.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是把两物放入关系中的平实动作。

items.example: It marks the manner of measuring, not the measurement itself.
items.exampleCN: 它标记衡量的方式，而不是衡量结果。

definition_zh: 显著地；出乎意料地；出色地；罕见地
definition_en: to a striking degree, in a way that is worth noticing or surprising
core_image: 人群里一个完全静立不动的人，所有目光都被他吸过去
scene: 老桥的石拱被磨得发亮，缝隙里长满青苔，却连一块石头也没松动。The old stone bridge is remarkably well preserved after six centuries.
sceneCN: 这里指保存得好到令人惊叹（第 1 个义项：达到显著、引人注目的程度）；句意为这座老石桥历经六个世纪仍保存得极为完好。

pos.zh: 显著地；出乎意料地；出色地；罕见地

derivatives.zh: 非凡的；显著的；值得注意的

senses.title: To a striking degree
senses.definition: so much that it stands out and draws attention
senses.definitionCN: 程度大到足以突出、引人注意
senses.example: The bridge is remarkably well preserved.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥保存得非常好。
senses.why: Remarkable is what deserves a remark; the adverb says the degree is high enough that people would point it out.
senses.whyCN: remarkable 是「值得被评说」的；副词表示程度高到人们会指着它说。

senses.title: Surprisingly
senses.definition: in a way that contradicts what would normally be expected
senses.definitionCN: 与通常预期相反
senses.example: Remarkably, no one was hurt in the crash.
senses.exampleCN: 出乎意料的是，撞车中没有人受伤。
senses.why: The word can open a sentence and flag the surprise itself, because what deserves remark here is the gap from expectation.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以开句，直接标记惊讶本身，因为此处值得评说的是与预期的落差。

senses.title: Very well indeed
senses.definition: with an excellence that deserves praise
senses.definitionCN: 好到值得称赞的程度
senses.example: She performed remarkably in the final round.
senses.exampleCN: 她在最后一轮表现得很出色。
senses.why: Praise is a remark of approval, so the adverb naturally measures performance that earns comment.
senses.whyCN: 称赞是一种赞许性的评说，因此副词自然用来衡量值得被人议论的表现。

senses.title: Noticeably alike or different
senses.titleCN: 相似或相异得十分明显
senses.definition: to a degree that is immediately visible in a comparison
senses.definitionCN: 在比较中一眼就能看出的程度
senses.example: The two accounts are remarkably similar.
senses.exampleCN: 两份叙述相似得惊人。
senses.why: Comparison is where remark begins: the adverb marks a resemblance or a gap wide enough to be worth noting.
senses.whyCN: 比较正是「评说」的起点：副词标出大到值得记一笔的相似或落差。

senses.title: Unusually, in a rare amount
senses.titleCN: 罕见地（数量异常少或多）
senses.definition: in an amount rare for the context, often surprisingly small
senses.definitionCN: 数量在该语境下罕见，常指异常地少
senses.example: Remarkably little rain fell that winter.
senses.exampleCN: 那年冬天下的雨少得出奇。
senses.why: A quantity far from the norm is itself a remark, so the adverb can attach to little as easily as to well.
senses.whyCN: 远离常规的数量本身就是一则「评说」，因此副词既能接表示「好」的词，也能接表示「少」的词。

senses.title: As a strong intensifier
senses.definition: used before adjectives to strengthen them to a high degree
senses.definitionCN: 放在形容词前，把程度提到很高
senses.example: The engine is remarkably quiet at speed.
senses.exampleCN: 这台发动机在高速时安静得出奇。
senses.why: Once the word means worth remarking on, it can simply boost any adjective that names a surprising quality.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词意为「值得一说」，它就可以单纯加强任何表示惊人性质的形容词。

senses.title: In a way that invites admiration
senses.definition: so as to arouse admiration, often after a difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 令人赞叹，常用于经历困难之后
senses.example: The team recovered remarkably after the loss.
senses.exampleCN: 失利之后，这支队伍恢复得令人赞叹。
senses.why: The remark implied here is not neutral comment but admiration, which colours the adverb in narratives of recovery.
senses.whyCN: 此处隐含的评说不是中性的议论，而是赞叹，这给「恢复」类叙事中的副词染上色彩。

senses.title: Standing out from the rest
senses.definition: in a way that clearly separates the thing from its peers
senses.definitionCN: 把该事物与同类明显区分开来
senses.example: A remarkably clear photograph hung above the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 书桌上方挂着一张清晰得惊人的照片。
senses.why: To remark on something is to single it out, so the adverb can mark the one member of a set that draws the eye.
senses.whyCN: 评说某物就是把它们挑出来，因此副词可以标记一组中唯一抓住目光的那一个。

intro.en: Remarkably is remarkable plus -ly. Remark is re- used as an intensifier with mark, a sign or boundary of Germanic origin, related to Old Norse mork. The direct source is clear, but the deeper link to Latin margo is a reported relationship rather than a borrowed Latin word.
intro.cn: remarkably 是 remarkable 加 -ly。remark 由加强语气的 re- 与 mark「记号、边界」构成，mark 属日耳曼来源，与古诺尔斯语 mork 相关。直接来源清楚；它与拉丁语 margo 的关系只是学者报告的远亲关系，并非借自拉丁语的词。

items.en: Mark goes back to a Germanic word for a boundary or sign, the same one behind march, a border land.
items.cn: mark 追溯至日耳曼语表示边界或记号的词，同一个词也给出 march「边境地带」。

items.en: Old Norse mork, a boundary or forest mark, reinforces the English word during the Viking period.
items.cn: 古诺尔斯语 mork「边界、林地标记」在维京时期强化了英语中的这个词。

items.en: French remarquer, to note or point out, supplies the pattern for English remark in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 法语 remarquer「注意、指出」在十七世纪为英语 remark 提供了范式。

items.en: Remark enters English as both noun and verb, meaning a comment and the act of noticing.
items.cn: remark 以名词与动词两种身份进入英语，意为评语与注意的行为。

items.en: The adjective remarkable, worth remarking on, appears in the seventeenth century and quickly widens to mean striking.
items.cn: 形容词 remarkable「值得评说的」于十七世纪出现，很快扩展为「显著的」。

items.en: The adverb is a later formation whose exact first date is uncertain; it spreads in travel and science writing as a marker of surprise.
items.cn: 副词是较晚的构词，确切首见年代不确定；它作为惊讶标记在游记与科学写作中普及。

note.en: The first group shares the Germanic mark sign-root; the second group names degrees of striking quality without the notion of a mark.
note.cn: 第一组共享日耳曼语 mark「记号」词根；第二组表示「突出程度」的各种说法，但不带记号概念。

entries.definition: Worth remarking on; striking or unusual.
entries.definitionCN: 值得评说的；显著或不寻常的。

entries.definition: A comment, or to notice and say something.
entries.definitionCN: 评语，或注意到并说些什么。

entries.definition: Ordinary, with nothing worth pointing out.
entries.definitionCN: 平常的，没有值得指出之处。

entries.definition: Clearly noticeable, as if carrying a visible sign.
entries.definitionCN: 明显可见的，仿佛带着一个看得见的记号。

entries.definition: Noticeably, but without the surprise that remarkably carries.
entries.definitionCN: 明显地，但不带 remarkably 所含的惊讶。

entries.definition: So as to make a strong visual or mental impression.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈地给人视觉或心理印象。

entries.definition: In a way that goes against expectation.
entries.definitionCN: 以违背预期的方式。

entries.definition: Especially, in a way worth naming.
entries.definitionCN: 尤其，值得点名的。

entries.definition: Far beyond the ordinary degree.
entries.definitionCN: 远超平常程度。

entries.definition: In a way rare for this kind of thing.
entries.definitionCN: 在此类事物中少见地。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real mark sign-root, the real remark verb and the common fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的 mark「记号」词根、真实的 remark 动词与常见固定搭配。

normal.en: A mark is a sign you put on a thing so it will be noticed, so remarkable means marked for attention.
normal.cn: mark 是打在物件上让人看见的记号，因此 remarkable 就是「被标出来引人注意的」。

normal.en: Remark is both to notice and to say something, and remarkable is what makes people do both.
normal.cn: remark 既是注意也是开口说，而 remarkable 正是让人又要看又要说的东西。

normal.en: Remarkably little rain is a remark about a number, not about an opinion.
normal.cn: 「雨少得出奇」是对一个数字的评说，而不是对意见的评说。

normal.en: Unremarkable is the quiet twin: nothing to point at.
normal.cn: unremarkable 是它安静的孪生兄弟：没有什么可指的。

normal.en: Markedly means noticeably; remarkably adds the small gasp of surprise.
normal.cn: markedly 只是「明显地」；remarkably 多了一声小小的惊叹。

abstract.en: Whatever is worth a remark has already beaten the average in some direction.
abstract.cn: 任何值得被评说的东西，都已经在某个方向上赢了平均。

abstract.en: The word measures the distance between what happened and what we expected.
abstract.cn: 这个词量的是「发生的」与「我们预期的」之间的距离。

abstract.en: To mark something is to decide that the eye should stop there.
abstract.cn: 标记某物，就是决定让目光停在那里。

examples.en: The two manuscripts are remarkably close in wording.
examples.cn: 两份手稿的措辞惊人地接近。

examples.en: Remarkably, the engine started on the first attempt after ten years.
examples.cn: 出人意料的是，放了十年之后，发动机第一次就启动了。

examples.en: The patients responded remarkably to the low dose.
examples.cn: 患者对低剂量的反应异常良好。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「瑞马克布利」，mark 是记号：被人拿记号笔圈出来的，就是显著地

root: remark = 加强语气前缀 re- + mark「记号、边界」（日耳曼来源，与古诺尔斯语 mork 相关；与拉丁语 margo 的关联只是远亲关系，不构成拉丁同族词）→ remarkable「值得评说的」→ 加 -ly 成副词。直接来源清楚，副词首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of one measuring stick: a high degree, a gap from expectation, an excellence worth praise, a visible resemblance, a rare quantity, a stronger adjective, an admired recovery, and one item singled out from its set.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共用同一把尺：很高的程度、与预期的落差、值得称赞的出色、看得见的相似、罕见的数量、更强的形容词、令人赞叹的复原，以及从同类中被挑出的那一个。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one person standing perfectly still in a moving crowd, and every eye goes there.
core.cn: 核心意象：流动的人群里一个完全静立的人，所有目光都被吸过去。

branches.en: THE DEGREE: high enough that people would point it out.
branches.cn: 程度：高到人们会指着它说。

branches.en: THE GAP: surprise at the start of a sentence, and the plain strengthening of an adjective.
branches.cn: 落差：句子开头的惊讶，以及对形容词的单纯加强。

branches.en: THE PRAISE: performance that earns comment, and recovery that earns admiration.
branches.cn: 赞许：值得议论的表现，以及值得赞叹的复原。

branches.en: THE COMPARISON: a likeness or difference wide enough to be worth a remark.
branches.cn: 比较：大到值得评说的相似或差异。

branches.en: THE OUTLIER: a quantity far from the norm, and one member that draws the eye.
branches.cn: 离群者：远离常规的数量，以及抓住目光的那一个成员。

intro.en: Remarkably is -ly on remarkable, and remarkable is re- plus mark plus -able. Mark is Germanic, so there is no Latin root here; only French remarquer shaped the English word.
intro.cn: remarkably 是 -ly 加在 remarkable 上，而 remarkable 是 re- 加 mark 再加 -able。mark 属日耳曼语，因此这里没有拉丁词根；只有法语 remarquer 塑造了英语这个词。

latinIntro.en: No Latin entries are listed. Mark is a Germanic sign word, reinforced by Old Norse, and French remarquer merely supplied the English pattern with a prefix.
latinIntro.cn: 此处不列拉丁词条。mark 是日耳曼语的「记号」词，受古诺尔斯语强化，法语 remarquer 只是带着前缀给英语提供了构词范式。

items.example: The core image of the word is a sign left so that others will notice.
items.exampleCN: 这个词的核心意象是留下一个让别人注意到的记号。

items.example: Here it strengthens rather than repeats the act of marking.
items.exampleCN: 此处它加强而非重复「做记号」这一动作。

items.example: To remark is to put a mental mark beside something.
items.exampleCN: 评说就是在某物旁边做一个心里的记号。

items.example: The suffix turns the comment into a quality of the thing.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「评说」变成事物自身的性质。

items.example: The adjective is the base of the adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是副词的构词基础。

items.example: It reports the degree that makes a thing worth a remark.
items.exampleCN: 它报告的是让某物值得一说的那个程度。

items.example: The negative prefix removes the reason to point.
items.exampleCN: 否定前缀拿掉了「值得指出来」的理由。

items.example: The cousin adverb measures visibility without surprise.
items.exampleCN: 这个同族副词只量「看得见」，不带惊讶。

items.example: French supplies the pattern that English remark follows.
items.exampleCN: 法语提供了英语 remark 所遵循的范式。

definition_zh: 具体地；专门地；确切地说；特定地
definition_en: in a precise, clearly limited way, or for one particular purpose
core_image: 一圈光斑只照在众多物件中的一件上
scene: 实验室里摆着一台仪器，它只测水温，别的什么都不做。The device was specifically built to measure water temperature in the field.
sceneCN: 这里指专为某一用途而造（第 2 个义项：为特定目的专门地）；句意为这台装置是专为野外测量水温而制造的。

pos.zh: 具体地；专门地；确切地说；特定地

senses.title: In precise detail
senses.definition: naming the exact thing rather than speaking in general
senses.definitionCN: 点出确切的对象，而不是笼统地说
senses.example: The report does not say specifically which sites were tested.
senses.exampleCN: 报告没有具体说明测试了哪些场地。
senses.why: Specificus in medieval Latin means making a particular kind, so the adverb points to one member instead of the class.
senses.whyCN: 中古拉丁语 specificus 意为「构成某一类的」，因此副词指向类中的一个成员，而不是整类。

senses.title: For one particular purpose
senses.definition: so as to serve one stated use and no other
senses.definitionCN: 为所述用途服务，不作他用
senses.example: The wing is specifically designed for low-speed flight.
senses.exampleCN: 这片机翼是专为低速飞行设计的。
senses.why: Once a thing is made for a kind, it is made for that kind alone, which is why the word marks purpose-built equipment.
senses.whyCN: 一物既为某一类而造，就只为那一类而造，这正是这个词标记「专用设备」的原因。

senses.title: To be exact, namely
senses.definition: used to introduce the exact item after a general statement
senses.definitionCN: 在笼统陈述之后引出确切项
senses.example: Specifically, three factors explain the gap.
senses.exampleCN: 具体说来，有三个因素解释了这一差距。
senses.why: As a sentence opener it narrows the previous clause to a list, acting like a spotlight switched on.
senses.whyCN: 作句首时，它把前一从句收窄成一份清单，像一盏灯突然打亮。

senses.title: Of a particular kind, not general
senses.titleCN: 特定类型的，而非一般性的
senses.definition: belonging to a limited type rather than to everything of that sort
senses.definitionCN: 属于有限类型，而不是该类的全部
senses.example: The drug targets a specifically human protein.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药针对一种人类特有的蛋白质。
senses.why: The word divides a general category into named sub-kinds and works only inside the named one.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把一个大类切成有名字的子类，并且只在被点名的子类里起作用。

senses.title: By name
senses.definition: so that a person or thing is named rather than covered by a general phrase
senses.definitionCN: 点到具体的人或物，而不是用泛称覆盖
senses.example: The contract names him specifically as the responsible party.
senses.exampleCN: 合同点名他为责任方。
senses.why: Naming is the clearest act of making a kind: a general term is replaced by a proper one.
senses.whyCN: 点名是「划出类别」最清楚的动作：泛称被专名替换。

senses.title: Limited to one tissue or species
senses.definition: in biology, active in one tissue, organ or species and not in others
senses.definitionCN: 生物学上指只在某一组织、器官或物种中起作用
senses.example: The enzyme is specifically active in root tissue.
senses.exampleCN: 这种酶只在根部组织中起作用。
senses.why: Biology needs a word for restriction to one site, and specificus already means belonging to a kind.
senses.whyCN: 生物学需要一个表示「只限于一处」的词，而 specificus 本已意为「属于某一类的」。

senses.title: In the technical sense
senses.definition: used in its technical meaning rather than its everyday one
senses.definitionCN: 按术语义使用，而非日常义
senses.example: The term is used specifically, not in its everyday sense.
senses.exampleCN: 这个词是按术语义使用的，不是日常义。
senses.why: A term with a narrow definition is specific, so the adverb warns the reader to stay inside that definition.
senses.whyCN: 定义狭窄的术语本身就是「特定」的，因此副词提醒读者留在这个定义之内。

senses.title: Uniquely associated with one group
senses.definition: as an exclusive feature found only in the stated group
senses.definitionCN: 作为只在所述群体中出现的独有特征
senses.example: This behaviour is specifically associated with the northern population.
senses.exampleCN: 这种行为与北方种群特有地相关。
senses.why: When a feature appears in one group and nowhere else, the adverb marks the boundary of the kind.
senses.whyCN: 当一个特征只出现在一个群体、别处都没有，副词就标出了这个类别的边界。

intro.en: Specifically is specific plus -ly. Specific is medieval Latin specificus, built from species, kind or appearance, and facere, to make, so the adjective means making a particular kind. The direct source is clear; the English date is approximate.
intro.cn: specifically 是 specific 加 -ly。specific 出自中古拉丁语 specificus，由 species「种类、外观」与 facere「制造」构成，故形容词意为「构成某一类的」。直接来源清楚，英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: Specere means to look, and it gives species, specimen, spectrum and inspect.
items.cn: specere 意为看，给出 species、specimen、spectrum 与 inspect。

items.en: Species first means appearance or sight, then a kind or sort, the sense that matters for specific.
items.cn: species 先指外观、所见，后指种类，后者正是 specific 所要用的义。

items.en: Scholastic Latin builds specificus, making a kind, to describe what marks off one sort of thing from another.
items.cn: 经院拉丁语造出 specificus「构成一类的」，用来描述把某一种事物与另一种区分开的东西。

items.en: English takes specific in the sixteenth century, first of medicines acting on one disease, then of anything precisely limited.
items.cn: 英语于十六世纪借入 specific，先指针对某一种病的药，后指任何限定精确之物。

items.en: The verb specify and the noun specification grow beside the adjective in legal and technical writing.
items.cn: 动词 specify 与名词 specification 在法律与技术文本中于形容词旁生长出来。

items.en: The adverb specifically becomes common in academic and legal prose; its exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 副词 specifically 在学术与法律文字中普及，确切首见年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the specere looking-root; the second group names precision and particularity without the image of looking.
note.cn: 第一组共享 specere「看」的词根；第二组表示精确与特定，但不带「看」的意象。

entries.definition: Clearly defined or belonging to one kind.
entries.definitionCN: 界定清楚或属于某一类的。

entries.definition: To state exactly, item by item.
entries.definitionCN: 逐项精确说明。

entries.definition: A detailed written statement of requirements.
entries.definitionCN: 详细写明要求的文件。

entries.definition: A kind of living thing; the Latin word behind specific.
entries.definitionCN: 一类生物；specific 背后的拉丁词。

entries.definition: Distinct or exceptional, from species through a different adjective path, not a form of specific.
entries.definitionCN: 独特或特别的，由 species 走另一条形容词路径而来，不是 specific 的变形。

entries.definition: Exactly, with no vagueness.
entries.definitionCN: 确切地，毫不含糊。

entries.definition: In clear words that leave nothing implied.
entries.definitionCN: 用清楚的字句说明，不留暗示。

entries.definition: With complete accuracy, neither more nor less.
entries.definitionCN: 完全准确，不多不少。

entries.definition: Singling out one case from a larger set.
entries.definitionCN: 从更大的集合中点出某一例。

entries.definition: Especially, or in a detailed way.
entries.definitionCN: 尤其，或以详细的方式。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real species and facere roots, the real taxonomy term and the real contract phrasing.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的 species 与 facere 词根、真实的分类学术语与真实的合同表述。

normal.en: Species is a kind, so specifically means pointing at one kind out of many.
normal.cn: species 是种类，所以 specifically 就是从许多类里指向一类。

normal.en: Facere is to make, and specificus means making a kind: the word itself does the sorting.
normal.cn: facere 是制造，specificus 意为「造出一个类」：这个词本身就在做分类。

normal.en: Specific medicine in older English meant a drug for one disease only, which is still the clearest picture.
normal.cn: 旧英语里的 specific medicine 指只治一种病的药，至今仍是最清楚的画面。

normal.en: More specifically is the writer's spotlight: it narrows the sentence to one item.
normal.cn: more specifically 是作者的聚光灯：把句子收窄到一项。

normal.en: Special and specific are cousins, not twins: special means exceptional, specific means clearly limited.
normal.cn: special 与 specific 是表亲不是双胞胎：前者指特别，后者指界定清楚。

abstract.en: A narrow beam is useful only because everything outside it is dark.
abstract.cn: 一束窄光之所以有用，只因为光束之外都是暗的。

abstract.en: Naming one thing is a way of agreeing to forget the rest for a moment.
abstract.cn: 点出一物，是一种约定暂时忘掉其余的方式。

abstract.en: Precision costs breadth, and the word is honest about the price.
abstract.cn: 精确要以广度为代价，这个词对这笔代价是诚实的。

examples.en: The rules apply specifically to part-time staff.
examples.cn: 这些规定专门适用于兼职人员。

examples.en: She asked specifically for the earlier version of the map.
examples.cn: 她点名要那幅较早的地图。

examples.en: More specifically, the loss came from two faulty seals.
examples.cn: 更具体地说，损失来自两个失效的密封件。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「斯佩西菲克利」，species 是「物种」：从一大堆里点到那一个物种，就是具体地

root: 拉丁语 specere「看」→ species「外观、种类」；中古拉丁语 specificus「构成一类的」= species + facere「制造」→ 英语 specific，再加 -ly 成副词。直接来源清楚；英语首见年代为约数。special 亦出自 species 但走另一条形容词路径，与 specific 不是同一形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all narrow the field: exact detail, one purpose, a list after a general claim, a limited sub-kind, a name, one tissue, a technical definition, and an exclusive group.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在收窄范围：确切细节、唯一用途、笼统陈述后的清单、有限的子类、一个名字、一处组织、一条术语定义，以及一个专属群体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a circle of light falling on one object among many.
core.cn: 核心意象：一圈光只落在众多物件中的一件上。

branches.en: THE EXACT ITEM: detail named outright, and the list that follows a general claim.
branches.cn: 确切项：直接点出的细节，以及笼统陈述之后的那份清单。

branches.en: THE ONE PURPOSE: built for a single stated use.
branches.cn: 唯一用途：为某一所述用途而造。

branches.en: THE SUB-KIND: a limited type, and a tissue or species that alone responds.
branches.cn: 子类：有限类型，以及唯一会起反应的组织或物种。

branches.en: THE NAME: a general phrase replaced by a proper one.
branches.cn: 名字：泛称被专名替换。

branches.en: THE BOUNDARY: a term kept inside its definition, and a feature found in one group only.
branches.cn: 边界：留在定义内的术语，以及只在一个群体出现的特征。

intro.en: Specifically is -ly on specific, and specific is medieval Latin specificus, from species plus facere. The looking-root specere sits behind species.
intro.cn: specifically 是 -ly 加在 specific 上，而 specific 是中古拉丁语 specificus，由 species 加 facere 构成。「看」的词根 specere 就在 species 背后。

latinIntro.en: Specere, to look, yields species, a sight or kind; facere, to make, turns that kind into specificus, making a kind.
latinIntro.cn: specere「看」给出 species「所见、种类」；facere「制造」把这个类别变成 specificus「构成一类的」。

items.example: The root also gives inspect and spectacle.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也给出 inspect 与 spectacle。

items.example: The noun shifts from what is seen to the sort that is seen.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词从「所见之物」转向「所见的种类」。

items.example: The verb supplies the making in specificus.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供 specificus 中的「制造」。

items.example: It also appears in scientific and terrific.
items.exampleCN: 它也出现在 scientific 与 terrific 中。

items.example: Scholastic writers use it to divide one sort from another.
items.exampleCN: 经院作者用它把一种与另一种分开。

items.example: English first applies it to remedies for one disease.
items.exampleCN: 英语最初把它用在只治一种病的药上。

items.example: The verb is the act of narrowing that the adverb reports.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词正是副词所报告的那次收窄。

items.example: Engineering turns the verb into a document.
items.exampleCN: 工程领域把这个动词变成一份文件。

items.example: The adverb marks the narrowing in speech.
items.exampleCN: 副词在言语中标出收窄的动作。

items.example: It shares species but not the -fic element, so it is no twin.
items.exampleCN: 它与 specific 共享 species，但不带 -fic 成分，因此不是孪生形式。

definition_en: after something else in time, without saying that the first thing caused the second
core_image: 一串按顺序落下的骨牌，后一块只是接着前一块倒下
scene: 雨停之后，村口的小桥先被修好，接着仓库才重新开门。The bridge was repaired first, and the warehouse reopened subsequently.
sceneCN: 这里指在修桥之后接着发生（第 1 个义项：时间上位于某事之后）；句意为桥先修好，仓库随后才重新开门。

pos.zh: 随后；之后；继而（只标时间先后，不标因果）

derivatives.zh: 后果（同出 sequi，但用 con- 前缀）

senses.title: Later in time
senses.definition: after an earlier event, seen from the standpoint of that earlier event
senses.definitionCN: 在较早事件之后，以那一事件为立足点看
senses.example: The first trial failed; the method was subsequently revised.
senses.exampleCN: 第一次试验失败，方法随后被修订。
senses.why: Subsequi is sub-, under or after, plus sequi, to follow: the word puts one event behind another on a timeline and says nothing about why.
senses.whyCN: subsequi 是 sub-「在后」加 sequi「跟随」：这个词把一个事件排在另一个之后，且对原因一字不提。

senses.title: Later in the telling
senses.definition: used in narrative to move the story to a later point
senses.definitionCN: 叙事中把情节推到较晚的时间点
senses.example: Subsequently, the company expanded into three provinces.
senses.exampleCN: 后来，这家公司扩展到了三个省。
senses.why: Narrative order is the same following relation applied to sentences, so the adverb can simply advance the story.
senses.whyCN: 叙述顺序就是把同一个「跟随」关系用在句子上，因此副词可以单纯把故事往前推。

senses.title: After a step in a procedure
senses.definition: used when one stage of a process comes after another in fixed order
senses.definitionCN: 指流程中一阶段按固定顺序排在另一阶段之后
senses.example: The samples were dried and subsequently weighed.
senses.exampleCN: 样品先烘干，随后称重。
senses.why: Laboratory steps follow one another by protocol, which is sequence as rule rather than sequence as accident.
senses.whyCN: 实验步骤按规程相互跟随，这是规则性的先后，而不是偶然的先后。

senses.title: In a later version
senses.definition: used of a text, rule or design that was changed at a later date
senses.definitionCN: 指文本、规则或设计在较晚时候被改动
senses.example: The rule was subsequently amended twice.
senses.exampleCN: 这条规则后来被修改了两次。
senses.why: Versions stack in time, and the word marks the later layer without judging whether the change was an improvement.
senses.whyCN: 版本按时间叠放，这个词标出较晚的那一层，并不评判改动是好是坏。

senses.title: Later in the course of a process
senses.definition: used of effects or symptoms that appear well after the start
senses.definitionCN: 指在开始之后很久才出现的效应或症状
senses.example: Symptoms appeared subsequently, weeks after exposure.
senses.exampleCN: 症状随后出现，在接触之后数周。
senses.why: Medicine separates exposure from onset, and the word marks the second point on that line.
senses.whyCN: 医学把接触与发病分开，这个词标出这条线上的第二个点。

senses.title: Afterwards in formal records
senses.definition: used in legal and official prose with passive verbs to record a later step
senses.definitionCN: 在法律与公文里与被动式连用，记录较晚的一步
senses.example: The agreement was subsequently filed with the court.
senses.exampleCN: 该协议其后被提交法院备案。
senses.why: Official writing needs a neutral marker of order, since it must not imply that the later act was caused by the earlier one.
senses.whyCN: 公文需要一个中性的顺序标记，因为它不能暗示后一行为由前一行为造成。

senses.title: In later studies
senses.definition: used in research writing for work published after the original report
senses.definitionCN: 研究写作中指在最初报告之后发表的工作
senses.example: Two groups subsequently reported the same effect.
senses.exampleCN: 有两个团队随后报告了同样的效应。
senses.why: Citation order is chronological order, and the adverb keeps the later work from being read as a consequence of the first.
senses.whyCN: 引用顺序就是时间顺序，副词避免把后来的工作读成最初工作的结果。

senses.title: Next in a chain of events
senses.definition: used for the next event in a chain, with order but not causation implied
senses.definitionCN: 指链条中紧接着的事件，只含顺序、不含因果
senses.example: The storm passed, and the floods came subsequently.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴过去，洪水随后到来。
senses.why: Two events can stand next to each other on a timeline while remaining causally unrelated, which is exactly what the word allows.
senses.whyCN: 两个事件可以在时间线上紧挨着，却在因果上互不相干，这正是这个词所允许的。

intro.en: Subsequently is subsequent plus -ly, and subsequent is Latin subsequens, the participle of subsequi, to follow after, from sub- under or after and sequi to follow. The direct source is clear; only the English date is approximate.
intro.cn: subsequently 是 subsequent 加 -ly；subsequent 来自拉丁语 subsequens，即 subsequi「随后跟随」的分词，由 sub-「在后」与 sequi「跟随」构成。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: Sequi means to follow, and it gives English sequence, sequel, consequence and consecutive.
items.cn: sequi 意为跟随，给出英语 sequence、sequel、consequence 与 consecutive。

items.en: Sub- means under, and in time expressions it means after, as in subsequi.
items.cn: sub- 意为在下，用在时间表达中即「在后」，如 subsequi。

items.en: Subsequi means to follow after or come next, with no hint that the earlier thing produced the later one.
items.cn: subsequi 意为随后跟随、接着来，并不暗示前者产生了后者。

items.en: The participle subsequens, following after, passes into learned Latin and then into French and English as an adjective.
items.cn: 分词 subsequens「随后的」传入学术拉丁语，再经法语进入英语作形容词。

items.en: Subsequent is recorded in English in the fifteenth century, in chronicles and legal records of later events.
items.cn: subsequent 于十五世纪见于英语，用于编年史与记录后续事件的法律文书中。

items.en: The adverb subsequently spreads in official and scientific prose; its exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 副词 subsequently 在公文与科学文字中普及，确切首见年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the sequi following-root but splits into different prefixes, and consequently is the one that must not be swapped with subsequently. The second group names later time without the root.
note.cn: 第一组共享 sequi「跟随」词根，但分成不同前缀；其中 consequently 是绝不能与 subsequently 互换的那一个。第二组表示「后来的时间」，不带这个词根。

entries.definition: Coming after something else; the adjective behind the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 在另一事之后到来的；副词所依托的形容词。

entries.definition: As a result, from con- plus sequi; it states causation and cannot replace subsequently, which states time only.
entries.definitionCN: 因此、结果上，由 con- 加 sequi 构成；它陈述因果，不能替代只陈述时间的 subsequently。

entries.definition: A result that follows from something, not merely an event that comes later.
entries.definitionCN: 由某事件引出的结果，而不只是时间上更晚的事件。

entries.definition: A set of things arranged in order of time or logic.
entries.definitionCN: 按时间或逻辑顺序排列的一组事物。

entries.definition: Following one after another without a gap, built with con- and not with sub-.
entries.definitionCN: 一个接一个、中间无间隔，用 con- 而非 sub- 构成。

entries.definition: At a time after the present or the point mentioned.
entries.definitionCN: 在现在或所述时点之后。

entries.definition: At a later time, after what has just been mentioned.
entries.definitionCN: 在较晚时候，即刚提到的事之后。

entries.definition: The American spelling of afterwards, same meaning.
entries.definitionCN: afterwards 的美式拼写，意义相同。

entries.definition: At that time next in a narrative order.
entries.definitionCN: 叙事顺序中接下来的那个时候。

entries.definition: From that time onward, in formal prose.
entries.definitionCN: 自那时起，正式的书面说法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real sequi root, the real sub- prefix and the crucial contrast with consequently.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的 sequi 词根、真实的 sub- 前缀，以及与 consequently 的关键区别。

normal.en: Sequi is to follow, so subsequent means following after on the timeline.
normal.cn: sequi 是跟随，因此 subsequent 意为在时间线上跟在后面。

normal.en: Sub- is under, and in time it becomes after: the later event stands below the earlier one in the list.
normal.cn: sub- 是在下，用在时间上就成「之后」：较晚的事件在清单里排在较早的下面。

normal.en: Consequently has con-, which means together: it joins cause to result, so it is not a synonym.
normal.cn: consequently 带 con-「共同」：它把原因与结果连在一起，因此不是同义词。

normal.en: In lab reports, dry first and weigh subsequently: the word is a protocol marker.
normal.cn: 实验报告里先烘干、随后称重：这个词是规程的标记。

normal.en: Two teams subsequently reported the same effect: later, not because of, the first paper.
normal.cn: 两个团队随后报告同样效应：是时间上较晚，而不是因为第一篇论文。

abstract.en: A row of dominoes falling says nothing about who pushed the first one.
abstract.cn: 骨牌一路倒下，并不说明是谁推了第一块。

abstract.en: Order is the cheapest kind of meaning: it needs no explanation, only a clock.
abstract.cn: 顺序是最便宜的意义：不需要解释，只需要一只钟。

abstract.en: Saying 'after' carefully is a way of refusing to say 'because'.
abstract.cn: 谨慎地说「之后」，是一种拒绝说「因为」的方式。

examples.en: The site was closed in spring and subsequently reopened in autumn.
examples.cn: 该场地春季关闭，随后在秋季重新开放。

examples.en: The committee met twice and subsequently issued a short statement.
examples.cn: 委员会开了两次会，随后发表了一份简短声明。

examples.en: These figures were subsequently corrected in the second edition.
examples.cn: 这些数字在第二版中随后得到更正。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「萨布西昆特利」，sub 是「在下」：排在下面那一条，就是随后发生地

root: 拉丁语 sequi「跟随」（同族 sequence、sequel、consequence）→ sub-「在下、在后」+ sequi 得 subsequi「随后跟随」→ 分词 subsequens「随后的」→ 英语 subsequent，加 -ly 成副词。直接来源清楚；副词首见年代为约数。注意 consequi（con- + sequi）才是「因而导致」，subsequently 只标时间先后。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all place one thing after another: in time, in a story, in a procedure, in a revised version, in the course of an illness, in official records, in later papers, and in a chain of events. None of them claims that the first thing caused the second.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都只是把一物排在另一物之后：时间上、故事里、流程中、修订版里、病程中、公文里、后续论文里、事件链上。它们没有一个声称前者导致了后者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of dominoes falling in order, the later ones merely next.
core.cn: 核心意象：一串按顺序倒下的骨牌，后面的只是接着而已。

branches.en: THE TIMELINE: later in time, and later in the telling of events.
branches.cn: 时间线：时间上较晚，以及叙述中较晚。

branches.en: THE PROTOCOL: the fixed order of steps in a procedure.
branches.cn: 规程：流程中固定的步骤顺序。

branches.en: THE RECORD: a later version of a text, and a later filing in official papers.
branches.cn: 卷宗：文本的较晚版本，以及公文中的后续备案。

branches.en: THE DELAYED APPEARANCE: symptoms well after exposure, and results in later studies.
branches.cn: 延迟出现：接触之后很久才有症状，以及后续研究中的结果。

branches.en: THE NEXT LINK: an event following another with no causal claim attached.
branches.cn: 下一环：事件接着另一事件，但不附带因果主张。

intro.en: Subsequently is -ly on subsequent, which is Latin subsequens, from sub- plus sequi. The whole family shares sequi, to follow, and only the prefixes change the kind of following.
intro.cn: subsequently 是 -ly 加在 subsequent 上，而 subsequent 是拉丁语 subsequens，由 sub- 加 sequi 构成。整个词族共享 sequi「跟随」，只有前缀改变「跟随」的方式。

latinIntro.en: Sequi gives sequence and sequel; con- makes consequi, to follow as a result; sub- makes subsequi, to follow merely in time.
latinIntro.cn: sequi 给出 sequence 与 sequel；con- 构成 consequi「作为结果跟随」；sub- 构成 subsequi「只在时间上跟随」。

items.example: The root supplies the plain act of following.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「跟随」这一平实动作。

items.example: In time words it lays the later item under the earlier.
items.exampleCN: 在时间词里，它把较晚的一项放在较早的一项下面。

items.example: The verb orders events without explaining them.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词只排事件的顺序，不作解释。

items.example: The participle becomes the English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词成为英语的形容词。

items.example: The adjective modifies the later item directly.
items.exampleCN: 形容词直接修饰较晚的那一项。

items.example: The adverb puts the whole clause later in time.
items.exampleCN: 副词把整个从句放到较晚的时间。

items.example: This verb, not subsequi, stands behind consequently.
items.exampleCN: consequently 背后是这个词，而不是 subsequi。

items.example: The noun keeps the causal force that subsequently lacks.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词保留了 subsequently 所缺的因果力。

items.example: The noun names the order itself rather than one step in it.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指顺序本身，而不是顺序中的某一步。

items.example: The word survives in books and in medicine.
items.exampleCN: 这个词在书籍与医学中都还活着。

definition_en: for that reason; used to introduce a conclusion drawn from what has just been said
core_image: 两段链条扣在一起，前一段的末端正好接上后一段的起点
scene: 山口被大雪封住，车辆全被拦在半山腰，队伍只好绕远路。The pass was closed by snow; therefore the convoy took the longer road.
sceneCN: 这里指由封路这一原因推出绕路的结论（第 1 个义项：因果结论）；句意为山路因雪封闭，因此车队走了更远的那条路。

pos.zh: 因此；所以；故（连接性副词，引出由前文推出的结论）

derivatives.zh: 借此；由此（同构复合词，fore 换成 by）
为此（法律用语，与 therefore 的构词成分相同）
为何；原因（where + fore 的同构形式）

senses.title: For that reason
senses.definition: used to introduce a result that the previous statement provides the reason for
senses.definitionCN: 引出结果，而前面的陈述给出这一结果的理由
senses.example: The road was closed; therefore we took the longer route.
senses.exampleCN: 道路封闭了，因此我们走了更远的那条路。
senses.why: Therefore is there plus fore, for that: the word points back at the stated cause and presents what follows as owed to it.
senses.whyCN: therefore 是 there 加 fore「为此」：它回指已说出的原因，并把后文呈现为由那个原因所欠下的。

senses.title: The inevitable step in an argument
senses.titleCN: 论证中必然推出的结论
senses.definition: used in logic where the conclusion cannot be false if the premises are true
senses.definitionCN: 用于逻辑，当前提为真时结论不可能为假
senses.example: All men are mortal; Socrates is a man; therefore Socrates is mortal.
senses.exampleCN: 人皆有死；苏格拉底是人；因此苏格拉底有死。
senses.why: In a syllogism the word marks the forced last line, the point at which the premises hand over their conclusion.
senses.whyCN: 在三段论里，这个词标出被迫写下的最后一行，也就是前提交出结论的那一点。

senses.title: The conclusion of a proof
senses.definition: used in mathematics to introduce a result derived from earlier steps
senses.definitionCN: 数学中用于引出由前面步骤得到的结果
senses.example: The two triangles are congruent; therefore their angles are equal.
senses.exampleCN: 两个三角形全等，因此它们的角相等。
senses.why: Proof writing needs a visible hinge between the derivation and the result, and this is that hinge.
senses.whyCN: 证明写作需要在推导与结果之间有一个看得见的铰链，这个词就是那个铰链。

senses.title: The formal hence of legal prose
senses.definition: used in formal and legal writing to state a required consequence
senses.definitionCN: 在正式与法律文字中陈述必须产生的后果
senses.example: The defendant failed to appear; therefore the court proceeded.
senses.exampleCN: 被告未出庭，故法庭继续审理。
senses.why: Statutes chain a condition to a consequence, and the older register of the word suits that chain of obligation.
senses.whyCN: 法条把条件与后果串起来，而这个词较古的语体正适合这条义务链。

senses.title: For that purpose, in older English
senses.definition: archaic: for that purpose or to that end
senses.definitionCN: 古旧义：为了那个目的、朝向那个目标
senses.example: He laboured therefore that the work might be finished.
senses.exampleCN: 他为此辛勤劳作，好把那件工作完成。
senses.why: Fore once meant for or on account of, so the compound could carry purpose as well as cause; modern English keeps mainly the causal sense.
senses.whyCN: fore 旧有「为了、由于」之义，因此这个复合词既能表目的也能表原因；现代英语主要保留因果义。

senses.title: The close of a rebuttal
senses.definition: used to close an argument after the evidence has been weighed
senses.definitionCN: 在证据权衡完毕后用来收束论证
senses.example: The evidence is incomplete; therefore the claim cannot stand.
senses.exampleCN: 证据不完整，因此这一主张不能成立。
senses.why: Debate ends by naming what the audience must accept, and the word converts a review of evidence into a verdict.
senses.whyCN: 辩论以点明听众必须接受什么来收尾，这个词把对证据的回顾转成裁决。

senses.title: The inference in an experiment
senses.definition: used in reports to state what the data allow the authors to infer
senses.definitionCN: 在报告中陈述数据让作者能推出什么
senses.example: The readings were consistent; therefore the model was accepted.
senses.exampleCN: 读数一致，因此该模型被接受。
senses.why: Scientific style separates observation from inference, and the word marks the crossing point.
senses.whyCN: 科学文体把观察与推论分开，这个词标出跨越的那一点。

senses.title: The summing up in teaching
senses.definition: used in explanation to gather the previous points into one conclusion
senses.definitionCN: 在讲解中把前面的要点收拢成一个结论
senses.example: Therefore, the plan needs revision before the next stage.
senses.exampleCN: 因此，这项计划在进入下一阶段之前需要修订。
senses.why: Teaching needs a marker that says the scattered facts now add up, which is the conversational use of the same hinge.
senses.whyCN: 教学需要一个标记说「零散的事实到此合成一个结论」，这是同一个铰链的口语用法。

intro.en: Therefore is an English compound of there and fore, an old word for before or for that. It is Germanic, not Latin, and the Latin ergo is a counterpart rather than a source. The direct source is clear; the first date is approximate.
intro.cn: therefore 是英语复合词，由 there 与 fore 构成，fore 是表示「在前、为此」的古词。它属日耳曼语而非拉丁语，拉丁语 ergo 只是对应词而非来源。直接来源清楚，首见年代为约数。

items.en: There comes from Old English thær, the locative form meaning in that place, later extended to that point in speech.
items.cn: there 来自古英语 thær，本为「在那个地方」的处所形式，后来扩展到言语中的「那一点」。

items.en: Fore meant before or in front, and in phrases it could mean for that or on account of that.
items.cn: fore 意为在前，在短语中也可表「为了那个、由于那个」。

items.en: The two parts join as therfore in the Middle English period, keeping the pointing function of there.
items.cn: 两部分在中古英语时期合为 therfore，保留了 there 的回指功能。

items.en: Sixteenth-century prose fixes therefore as the standard marker of a conclusion, beside the older thus and hence.
items.cn: 十六世纪的印本散文把 therefore 固定为结论标记，与较早的 thus、hence 并列。

items.en: Modern English keeps therefore for logical consequence and therefor, a different spelling, for legal purpose.
items.cn: 现代英语用 therefore 表逻辑后果，而用拼写不同的 therefor 表法律上的目的。

note.en: The first group shares the there plus fore pattern and includes the look-alike therefor. The second group names conclusions and reasons, and includes consequently and subsequently, which differ in whether causation is claimed.
note.cn: 第一组共享 there + fore 的构词模式，并包含形近的 therefor。第二组表示结论与理由，其中 consequently 与 subsequently 的区别在于是否主张因果。

entries.definition: For that purpose, a legal spelling with one r fewer than therefore; it is not a misspelling of the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 为此目的，法律用语，比 therefore 少一个 r；它不是 therefore 的拼写错误。

entries.definition: By that means, with by in place of fore.
entries.definitionCN: 借此、由此，用 by 代替 fore。

entries.definition: Of that or of it, in legal and formal writing.
entries.definitionCN: 其、由此，用于法律与正式文字。

entries.definition: In that place or in that document.
entries.definitionCN: 在其中、在该文件之内。

entries.definition: For what reason, built on where instead of there, and preserved in legal and poetic prose.
entries.definitionCN: 为何、由于什么，用 where 而非 there 构成，存于法律与诗歌文字中。

entries.definition: In this way or as a result, often marking a conclusion in formal prose.
entries.definitionCN: 如此、因此，正式文字中常作结论标记。

entries.definition: From this fact, as a consequence; also from this time.
entries.definitionCN: 由此、因此；也表「从此时起」。

entries.definition: As a result; stronger on causation and weaker on argument than therefore.
entries.definitionCN: 结果上；比 therefore 更强调因果，论证色彩较弱。

entries.definition: In a way that matches what has just been said, often of action taken.
entries.definitionCN: 按照刚说的情况而行事。

entries.definition: Afterwards in time only; it never supplies the causal link that therefore carries.
entries.definitionCN: 只表时间上的随后；它从不提供 therefore 所带的因果连接。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real there plus fore pattern and keep therefore apart from subsequently and consequently.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的 there + fore 构词模式，并把 therefore 与 subsequently、consequently 区分开。

normal.en: There points back, fore means for: therefore is for that, pointing at the reason just given.
normal.cn: there 回指，fore 意为「为了」：therefore 就是「为此」，指向刚给出的理由。

normal.en: In a syllogism the word is the last line, the place where premises hand over their conclusion.
normal.cn: 在三段论里，这个词是最后一行，是前提交出结论的地方。

normal.en: Mathematicians write therefore where the proof turns from work to result.
normal.cn: 数学家在证明从推导转向结果的地方写 therefore。

normal.en: Then there is time, therefore is cause: one is a clock, the other a hinge.
normal.cn: then 是时间，therefore 是原因：一个是钟，一个是铰链。

normal.en: Lawyers keep therefor with one r for purpose, and therefore with two for conclusions.
normal.cn: 律师用少一个 r 的 therefor 表目的，用两个 r 的 therefore 表结论。

abstract.en: A conclusion is a debt the earlier sentence has already agreed to pay.
abstract.cn: 结论是前一句话已经答应偿付的一笔债。

abstract.en: Saying therefore is claiming that nothing else could have followed.
abstract.cn: 说「因此」，就是在主张不可能有别的结果。

abstract.en: The word works because two sentences can be made to touch.
abstract.cn: 这个词能起作用，只因为两句话可以被接得贴在一起。

examples.en: The sample was contaminated; therefore the results were discarded.
examples.cn: 样品被污染，因此结果作废。

examples.en: The two accounts disagree; therefore at least one is wrong.
examples.cn: 两种说法互相矛盾，因此至少有一种是错的。

examples.en: The bridge carries no traffic; therefore repairs can wait.
examples.cn: 这座桥不通车，因此修缮可以推迟。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「戴尔福」，there 指「那件事」，fore 指「为了」：为了那件事，所以如此

root: 英语复合词 there + fore（fore 古义为「在前、为了」）。属日耳曼语来源，拉丁语 ergo「因此」只是对应词而非词源，故不列拉丁同族。现代英语用 therefore 表逻辑后果，用拼写 therefor 表法律上的目的。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one hinge: something has been stated, and what follows is presented as owed to it. The setting changes from daily reasoning to syllogism, proof, statute, archaic purpose, rebuttal, experiment and classroom summary.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享一个铰链：某事已被陈述，后文被呈现为由它欠下的。场景从日常推理换到三段论、证明、法条、古旧的目的义、辩驳、实验与课堂总结。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two chains joined so that the end of one meets the beginning of the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条链条相接，前一条的末端正好扣住后一条的起点。

branches.en: THE EVERYDAY CAUSE: a result the previous sentence has already paid for.
branches.cn: 日常原因：前一语句已经付过账的结果。

branches.en: THE FORCED LINE: the last step of a syllogism, and the closing line of a proof.
branches.cn: 被迫的一行：三段论的最后一步，以及证明的收束句。

branches.en: THE STATUTE: a condition in law handing over a required consequence.
branches.cn: 法条：法律中的条件交出必须承担的后果。

branches.en: THE OLD PURPOSE: for that end, a sense modern English has mostly dropped.
branches.cn: 古旧目的义：为了那个目标，现代英语已大体舍弃。

branches.en: THE VERDICT: closing a rebuttal, crossing from data to inference, and summing up a lesson.
branches.cn: 裁决：收束辩驳、从数据跨到推论，以及总结一堂课。

intro.en: Therefore is not a suffixed word but a compound of there and fore. English reuses the same frame in thereby, therein, thereof and the legal therefor, and wherefore swaps where for there.
intro.cn: therefore 不是加后缀的词，而是 there 与 fore 的复合词。英语用同一框架造出 thereby、therein、thereof 与法律用语的 therefor，wherefore 则把 where 换到 there 的位置。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic and has no Latin cognate, so no Latin entries are listed. Latin ergo and igitur are counterparts in meaning only.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语，没有拉丁同族词，因此不列拉丁词条。拉丁语 ergo 与 igitur 只是在意义上对应。

items.meaning: in that place; at that point
items.meaningCN: 在那个地方；在那一点上
items.example: The first half of the compound is the pointing finger.
items.exampleCN: 复合词的前半截就是那根指过去的手指。

items.example: The second half supplies the sense of on account of.
items.exampleCN: 后半截提供「由于、为了」的意思。

items.example: The compound is fixed by the sixteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词在十六世纪固定下来。

items.example: Legal drafters keep the shorter spelling for purpose.
items.exampleCN: 法律起草者用较短的拼写表目的。

items.example: The frame swaps fore for by and keeps the pointing.
items.exampleCN: 这个框架把 fore 换成 by，回指功能不变。

items.example: The same slot also takes a preposition of place.
items.exampleCN: 同一个位置也可以放表示处所的前置词。

items.example: Contracts use the form to point back at a defined item.
items.exampleCN: 合同用它回指已定义的事项。

items.example: The interrogative version of the same frame survives in legal prose.
items.exampleCN: 同一框架的疑问版本存活于法律文字中。

items.example: It is the older rival that therefore largely displaced.
items.exampleCN: 它是 therefore 大体上取代了的较早对手。

items.example: It marks manner as well as conclusion, which therefore does not.
items.exampleCN: 它既标方式也标结论，而 therefore 不标方式。

definition_zh: 最终；归根结底；根本上；终极地
definition_en: at the end of a process, or when everything has been considered
core_image: 一条长路的尽头立着一块界碑，走过所有岔路才能看见
scene: 谈判从清晨拖到深夜，桌上的文件改了又改，最后签下的只有那一页。After a whole day of revisions, the negotiators ultimately signed a single page.
sceneCN: 这里指经过整日修改之后最终签下（第 1 个义项：时间终点上的「最终」）；句意为经过一整天的修改，谈判者最终只签了一页。

pos.zh: 最终；归根结底；根本上；终极地

derivatives.zh: 隐秘的；日后的（同出 ulter「在彼方」）

senses.title: At the end of a process
senses.definition: after everything else has happened, at the final point in time
senses.definitionCN: 在其余一切都发生之后，位于时间的最后一点
senses.example: Ultimately the project was abandoned.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目最终被放弃了。
senses.why: Ultimus is the Latin superlative of last, so the adverb marks the point beyond which the story does not go.
senses.whyCN: ultimus 是拉丁语「最后的」最高级，因此副词标出故事不再往前的那一点。

senses.title: When everything is weighed
senses.definition: when all arguments and details have been taken into account
senses.definitionCN: 在所有论据与细节都被考虑之后
