senses.example: Ultimately, the argument rests on one assumption.
senses.exampleCN: 归根结底，这个论证依赖一个假设。
senses.why: The last point in an analysis is the one that remains when earlier ones are set aside, which is why the word also means in the end.
senses.whyCN: 分析中的最后一点，是把前面各点搁置后仍然留下的那一点，所以这个词也表「说到底」。

senses.title: Fundamentally
senses.definition: in terms of the deepest or most basic cause
senses.definitionCN: 就最深、最基本的成因而言
senses.example: The problem is ultimately economic.
senses.exampleCN: 这个问题根本上是经济问题。
senses.why: What lies last in a chain of explanation is also the base that holds the rest up, so final and fundamental share one word.
senses.whyCN: 解释链条上的最后一环，也是撑住其余的底座，因此「最终」与「根本」共用一个词。

senses.title: As the final aim
senses.definition: as the purpose toward which a whole programme is directed
senses.definitionCN: 作为整个方案所朝向的目的
senses.example: The programme ultimately aims at full employment.
senses.exampleCN: 该方案最终目标是充分就业。
senses.why: An aim sits at the end of effort, so the superlative of last also names the goal that justifies the work.
senses.whyCN: 目的位于努力尽头，因此「最后」的最高级也命名那个使工作正当的目标。

senses.title: Tracing back to the earliest origin
senses.definition: used when following a thing back to its earliest known source
senses.definitionCN: 把某物追到已知的最早来源
senses.example: The custom derives ultimately from harvest rituals.
senses.exampleCN: 这一习俗最终源自收获祭仪。
senses.why: Going back far enough reaches a first point, and the word works in both directions: last in time, first in origin.
senses.whyCN: 回溯得足够远就到达第一个点，这个词两个方向都通：时间上的最后，起源上的最初。

senses.title: Holding final accountability
senses.definition: used of the person or body that answers for a whole system
senses.definitionCN: 指对整个体系负最终责任的人或机构
senses.example: The minister is ultimately responsible for the department.
senses.exampleCN: 部长对该部门负最终责任。
senses.why: Responsibility runs to the top of a hierarchy, and the top is where no further appeal is possible.
senses.whyCN: 责任沿层级向上归结，而顶层正是再无更高申诉之处。

senses.title: The decisive last word
senses.definition: used of the authority or decision that settles a matter
senses.definitionCN: 指对某事作出终结性裁定的权力或决定
senses.example: The board ultimately decides on the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 预算最终由董事会决定。
senses.why: A decision that ends the argument occupies the last slot, which the Latin superlative turns into a claim of finality.
senses.whyCN: 终结争论的决定占据最后一格，拉丁最高级把它变成一种终局性的主张。

senses.title: In the ultimate analysis of philosophy
senses.definition: used of a final cause or principle beyond which nothing can be traced
senses.definitionCN: 指无法再向前追溯的终极原因或原则
senses.example: Philosophers speak of an ultimately simple principle behind change.
senses.exampleCN: 哲学家谈论变化背后一个终极简单的原理。
senses.why: Philosophy needs a term for what admits no further reduction, and the superlative of last supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 哲学需要一个词表示不可再化简之物，而「最后」的最高级正好提供。

intro.en: Ultimately is ultimate plus -ly, and ultimate is Late Latin ultimatus, from ultimus, last or farthest, the superlative of ulter, beyond. The direct source is clear; only the first English date is approximate.
intro.cn: ultimately 是 ultimate 加 -ly；ultimate 出自晚期拉丁语 ultimatus，源自 ultimus「最后的、最远的」，即 ulter「在彼方的」最高级。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: Ulter means beyond or on the far side, and it also gives ulterior and the prefix ultra-.
items.cn: ulter 意为在彼方、在那一边，也给出 ulterior 与前缀 ultra-。

items.en: Ultimus is the superlative of ulter, the farthest one, hence the last in any order.
items.cn: ultimus 是 ulter 的最高级，意为最远者，因而也是任何顺序中的最后者。

items.en: Ultimatus, brought to the last point, is formed as a participle and passes into legal and scholastic use.
items.cn: ultimatus 意为「被推到最后一刻的」，以分词形式进入法律与经院用法。

items.en: Ultimate appears in English in the seventeenth century, first in theology and law as the final or basic term.
items.cn: ultimate 于十七世纪进入英语，先用于神学与法律，指最终或基本的项。

items.en: The noun ultimatum, a final demand, enters diplomacy in the eighteenth century from the same stem.
items.cn: 名词 ultimatum「最后通牒」于十八世纪由同一词干进入外交领域。

items.en: The adverb ultimately spreads in analysis and journalism; its exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 副词 ultimately 在分析与新闻写作中普及，确切首见年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the ultimus farthest-root, including penultimate and ultimatum. The second group names finality and basic causes without that root.
note.cn: 第一组共享 ultimus「最远」词根，包含 penultimate 与 ultimatum。第二组表示终局与根本原因，但不带这个词根。

entries.definition: Final, or most basic; also the best achievable.
entries.definitionCN: 最终的、最根本的；也指可达到的极致。

entries.definition: A final demand with a threat attached.
entries.definitionCN: 附带威胁的最后要求。

entries.definition: Second to last, from paene, almost, plus ultimus.
entries.definitionCN: 倒数第二的，由 paene「几乎」加 ultimus 构成。

entries.definition: Beyond what is stated, often of a hidden motive, from the same ulter.
entries.definitionCN: 超出所述之外的，常指隐藏动机，同出 ulter。

entries.definition: Beyond, as in ultraviolet and ultrasonic, from the same beyond-word.
entries.definitionCN: 超出，如 ultraviolet 与 ultrasonic，同出这个「在彼方」的词。

entries.definition: After a long time or a series of delays.
entries.definitionCN: 经过很长时间或一连串拖延之后。

entries.definition: At some later point, often after complications.
entries.definitionCN: 在较晚的某一点，常指经历曲折之后。

entries.definition: When everything has been settled.
entries.definitionCN: 一切尘埃落定之时。

entries.definition: At the level of basic principles.
entries.definitionCN: 在基本原则的层面上。

entries.definition: In reality, once appearances are removed.
entries.definitionCN: 去掉表象之后的实情。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real ultimus and ulter roots and the real legal and philosophical uses.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的 ultimus 与 ulter 词根，以及真实的法律与哲学用法。

normal.en: Ultimus is the farthest one, so ultimately means at the far end of the road.
normal.cn: ultimus 是最远者，所以 ultimately 意为在道路的最远端。

normal.en: Penultimate is almost last: paene means almost, and the last seat has a neighbour.
normal.cn: penultimate 是「几乎最后」：paene 意为几乎，最后一个座位也有邻居。

normal.en: An ultimatum is a final demand, the same lastness moved into diplomacy.
normal.cn: ultimatum 是最后通牒，同一个「最后」搬到外交场合。

normal.en: Ultimately responsible means there is no one further up to blame.
normal.cn: 「最终负责」意味着再往上一级已无人可归咎。

normal.en: Tracing back ultimately gives the earliest origin, while looking ahead gives the final result, both at the far end.
normal.cn: 往回追是「最终源自」，往前看是「最终结果」，两者都在最远端。

abstract.en: The end of the road is where all the branching paths stop pretending to differ.
abstract.cn: 路的尽头，是所有岔路不再假装彼此不同的地方。

abstract.en: What is ultimate cannot be argued with, because there is no further room to stand.
abstract.cn: 终极之物无法再被争辩，因为它之后没有可站的地方。

abstract.en: Every long explanation ends with one sentence that refuses to explain itself.
abstract.cn: 每一段漫长的解释，都以一句拒绝解释自己的话收尾。

examples.en: The dispute was ultimately settled out of court.
examples.cn: 这场纠纷最终在庭外和解。

examples.en: Ultimately, the design was limited by the material available.
examples.cn: 归根结底，这个设计受限于可获得的材料。

examples.en: These traditions derive ultimately from the same river valley.
examples.cn: 这些传统最终都源自同一个河谷。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「阿尔提美特利」，ultimate 是「终极」：走到路的尽头，就是最终地

root: 拉丁语 ulter「在彼方的」→ 最高级 ultimus「最远、最后」→ 晚期拉丁语 ultimatus → 英语 ultimate，加 -ly 成副词。直接来源清楚；副词首见年代为约数。同族 ultimatum、penultimate（paene「几乎」+ ultimus）与 ulterior、前缀 ultra- 均出自 ulter。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all stand at a far end: the end of time, the end of analysis, the base of a cause, the aim of a programme, the earliest origin, the top of accountability, the decisive word, and the point beyond which philosophy cannot go.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都站在某个远端：时间的尽头、分析的尽头、原因的底座、方案的目标、最早的来源、责任的顶端、定夺的一句话，以及哲学无法再越过的点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a boundary stone at the end of a long road, visible only after every fork has been passed.
core.cn: 核心意象：长路尽头的一块界碑，走完所有岔路才看得见。

branches.en: THE END IN TIME: the point after which the story does not continue.
branches.cn: 时间终点：故事不再往前的那一点。

branches.en: THE FINAL BALANCE: what remains after all is weighed, and the deepest cause beneath it.
branches.cn: 最终结算：一切权衡后仍留下者，以及它下面的最深成因。

branches.en: THE GOAL: the purpose at the end of effort, which justifies the work.
branches.cn: 目标：努力尽头的目的，它使工作获得理由。

branches.en: THE ORIGIN: the earliest source reached by tracing backward.
branches.cn: 起源：回溯所能到达的最早来源。

branches.en: NO APPEAL: accountability at the top, the decision that settles, and the principle that admits no reduction.
branches.cn: 不可再上诉：顶端的责任、终结争论的决定，以及不可化简的原理。

intro.en: Ultimately is -ly on ultimate, which is Late Latin ultimatus from ultimus, the superlative of ulter. The beyond-word also yields ultra- and ulterior.
intro.cn: ultimately 是 -ly 加在 ultimate 上，而 ultimate 是晚期拉丁语 ultimatus，出自 ulter 的最高级 ultimus。这个「在彼方」的词也给出 ultra- 与 ulterior。

latinIntro.en: Ulter and its superlative ultimus carry the idea of the far side; -atus and English -ly only adjust the word class.
latinIntro.cn: ulter 及其最高级 ultimus 承载「彼方」之义；-atus 与英语 -ly 只调整词类。

items.example: The stem supplies the idea of distance rather than rank.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干提供的是距离感，而不是等级感。

items.example: Distance becomes order: the farthest is also the last.
items.exampleCN: 距离变成顺序：最远的也就是最后的。

items.example: Legal Latin uses it for a final act or final demand.
items.exampleCN: 法律拉丁语用它指最后的行为或最后的要求。

items.example: English applies it to causes, goals and authority.
items.exampleCN: 英语把它用在原因、目标与权力上。

items.example: The adverb reports the point the whole chain reaches.
items.exampleCN: 副词报告整条链条所抵达的点。

items.example: Diplomacy turns the lastness into a threat with a deadline.
items.exampleCN: 外交把「最后」变成带期限的威胁。

items.example: Paene, almost, stops the word one place short.
items.exampleCN: paene「几乎」让这个词在最后一格之前停下。

items.example: The same beyond-word comes to mean a motive kept out of sight.
items.exampleCN: 同一个「彼方」之词转指被藏在视线之外的动机。

items.example: The prefix marks what lies past a limit, as in ultraviolet.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出越过界限之物，如 ultraviolet。

items.example: It makes the adjective into a statement about when or how far.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词变成关于时间或远近的陈述。

definition_en: with near certainty; used to say that something is not open to reasonable doubt
core_image: 两个人站在岔路口犹豫，第三个人已经径直走过，不再回头看
scene: 窑火已经熄了整夜，窑口却还烫手，老匠人说这是多年来最好的一窑。The kiln had cooled all night, yet it was undoubtedly the best firing in years.
sceneCN: 这里指对评价有接近确定的把握（第 1 个义项：毫无疑问地）；句意为窑已冷却整夜，但这无疑是多年来最好的一窑。

pos.zh: 毫无疑问地；无疑；必定（确定度接近断言，而非推测）

senses.title: Beyond reasonable doubt
senses.definition: used to state that something is certain enough to exclude reasonable doubt
senses.definitionCN: 表示某事确定到足以排除合理怀疑
senses.example: Undoubtedly, the discovery changed the field.
senses.exampleCN: 毫无疑问，这一发现改变了该领域。
senses.why: The un- prefix cancels doubt outright, and the -ed adjective makes the absence of doubt a settled state rather than a hope.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 un- 直接取消怀疑，-ed 形容词又把「无怀疑」变成已定的状态，而非一种期望。

senses.title: A confident assertion
senses.definition: used when the speaker commits fully to a judgement
senses.definitionCN: 说话人对某一判断作出完全承诺时使用
senses.example: She is undoubtedly the best candidate.
senses.exampleCN: 她无疑是最佳人选。
senses.why: Certainty here is a claim about the speaker's commitment, stronger than probably and unlike presumably, which infers from likelihood.
senses.whyCN: 这里的确定是对说话人承诺程度的声明，强于 probably，也不同于 presume 一类由可能性作出的推断。

senses.title: Not open to dispute
senses.definition: used of a fact or finding that no serious objection can touch
senses.definitionCN: 指没有严肃反对能够动摇的事实或结论
senses.example: The evidence is undoubtedly genuine.
senses.exampleCN: 这证据无疑是真实的。
senses.why: When doubt is removed rather than merely reduced, the statement claims the end of argument, not a high probability.
senses.whyCN: 当怀疑是被取消、而不只是被减弱，这句话主张的是争论的终结，而不是一个高概率。

senses.title: Evidently, on the face of it
senses.definition: used of what is plain to any observer
senses.definitionCN: 指任何观察者都看得明白的事
senses.example: Undoubtedly he knew the risk he was taking.
senses.exampleCN: 他显然知道自己承担的风险。
senses.why: What is visible to everyone needs no argument, so the adverb can mean plainly rather than beyond all possible doubt.
senses.whyCN: 人人可见之事无需论证，因此副词可以指「明摆着」，而不必是排除一切可能的怀疑。

senses.title: Uses in concession
senses.definition: used to grant a point before turning against it
senses.definitionCN: 先承认一点，随即转回反对
senses.example: Undoubtedly the plan has costs, but the alternative is worse.
senses.exampleCN: 诚然这项计划有代价，但替代方案更糟。
senses.why: Granting certainty about the opponent's point costs nothing and buys the right to disagree on other grounds.
senses.whyCN: 承认对方所言之确定，代价很小，却换来在别处反驳的权利。

senses.title: Strengthening a superlative
senses.definition: used before a superlative to insist on the top of the scale
senses.definitionCN: 放在最高级之前，强调刻度顶端
senses.example: This is undoubtedly the finest example in the collection.
senses.exampleCN: 这无疑是藏品中最精美的一件。
senses.why: If the top of a scale is already unique, the adverb only removes the last flicker of hesitation about it.
senses.whyCN: 既然刻度顶端本就唯一，副词只是去掉关于它的最后一点迟疑。

senses.title: Publicly acknowledged
senses.definition: used of a standing that everyone in the field already accepts
senses.definitionCN: 指该领域所有人都已接受的声望或地位
senses.example: She is undoubtedly regarded as the founder of the field.
senses.exampleCN: 她被公认为这个领域的奠基人。
senses.why: When no one in the relevant community would object, the absence of doubt is social rather than personal.
senses.whyCN: 当相关群体中无人会反对时，这份「无疑」是社会性的，而不是个人性的。

senses.title: Confident about what has happened
senses.titleCN: 对已发生之事的高确定推断
senses.definition: used of an inference about the past that the speaker treats as settled
senses.definitionCN: 指对过去情况的推断，说话人把它当作已经确定
senses.example: By now the train has undoubtedly left the platform.
senses.exampleCN: 到这会儿，火车无疑已经离站了。
senses.why: This is still an inference, but it is stated as a conclusion rather than as a likelihood, which is where it parts company with presumably.
senses.whyCN: 这仍是推断，但被说成结论而不是可能性，这正是它与 presumably 分道的地方。

intro.en: Undoubtedly is un- plus doubted plus -ly, and doubt comes from Latin dubitare, to waver, from dubius, doubtful, probably from duo, two, the mind pulled both ways. The direct source is clear; the silent b was restored in spelling under Latin influence.
intro.cn: undoubtedly 是 un- 加 doubted 再加 -ly；doubt 出自拉丁语 dubitare「摇摆」，源于 dubius「可疑的」，一般认为出自 duo「二」，指心思被拉向两边。直接来源清楚；不发音的 b 是受拉丁语影响在拼写上补回的。

items.en: Duo means two, and dubius is usually explained as a state of being pulled between two options.
items.cn: duo 意为二，dubius 一般被解释为被两个选项拉来拉去的状态。

items.en: Dubitare means to hesitate or waver, and it also gives dubiety and indubitable.
items.cn: dubitare 意为犹豫、摇摆，也给出 dubiety 与 indubitable。

items.en: Old French doutier drops the Latin b in sound, and English borrows the word without it.
items.cn: 古法语 doutier 在读音中丢掉了拉丁语的 b，英语借入时也不带它。

items.en: Sixteenth-century writers reinsert b in the spelling to show the Latin origin, though the letter stays silent.
items.cn: 十六世纪作者在拼写上补回 b 以示拉丁来源，尽管这个字母并不发音。

items.en: The adjective undoubted, not doubted, appears in the fifteenth century and means settled beyond question.
items.cn: 形容词 undoubted「不被怀疑的」于十五世纪出现，意为已定、不容置疑。

items.en: The adverb undoubtedly becomes common in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries; its exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 副词 undoubtedly 在十八、十九世纪普及，确切首见年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the dubitare wavering-root, including indubitable and dubiety. The second group ranks confidence, and the entries for presumably and arguably mark weaker, inferential claims that undoubtedly must not be confused with.
note.cn: 第一组共享 dubitare「摇摆」词根，含 indubitable 与 dubiety。第二组给出确定度的阶梯，其中 presumably 与 arguably 是较弱的推断性说法，不能与 undoubtedly 混用。

entries.definition: Not questioned; accepted as certain.
entries.definitionCN: 不受质疑的；被认作确定的。

entries.definition: Uncertainty, or to question whether something is true.
entries.definitionCN: 不确定，或质疑某事是否真实。

entries.definition: Open to question; unlikely.
entries.definitionCN: 可质疑的；不太可能的。

entries.definition: Certainly; also an adjective meaning certain, built with -less instead of -ed.
entries.definitionCN: 无疑；也作形容词表确定，用 -less 而非 -ed 构成。

entries.definition: The state of being doubtful, from Latin dubietas.
entries.definitionCN: 存疑的状态，出自拉丁语 dubietas。

entries.definition: Impossible to doubt, built with in- on the Latin stem rather than with English un-.
entries.definitionCN: 不可能被怀疑的，用 in- 加拉丁词干，而非英语 un-。

entries.definition: Without doubt, said of a fact or a promise.
entries.definitionCN: 毫无疑问，用于事实或承诺。

entries.definition: With full commitment, often answering a question.
entries.definitionCN: 完全肯定，常用于回答问题。

entries.definition: As may reasonably be supposed; an inference from likelihood, not an assertion of certainty.
entries.definitionCN: 据合理推测；由可能性作出的推断，而不是确定断言。

entries.definition: As can be supported by argument, leaving the dispute open.
entries.definitionCN: 如论证所能支持的那样，仍留有争论空间。

entries.definition: More likely than not, without claiming certainty.
entries.definitionCN: 很可能，但不断言确定。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real dubitare root, the silent b and the ladder of certainty that separates undoubtedly from presumably.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的 dubitare 词根、不发音的 b，以及把 undoubtedly 与 presumably 分开的确定度阶梯。

normal.en: Dubius is the mind pulled two ways, so doubt is literally standing at a fork.
normal.cn: dubius 是心思被拉向两边的状态，因此怀疑字面上就是站在岔路口。

normal.en: The b in doubt is silent and was put back by Latin-loving printers.
normal.cn: doubt 里的 b 不发音，是喜爱拉丁文的印书人补回去的。

normal.en: Un- cancels the fork: there is no second way left to stand.
normal.cn: un- 取消了这个岔路：再没有第二条路可站。

normal.en: Presumably is a guess about likelihood; undoubtedly is a refusal to leave the matter open.
normal.cn: presumably 是对可能性的猜测；undoubtedly 是拒绝把这件事留作未定。

normal.en: Arguably keeps the argument alive; undoubtedly ends it.
normal.cn: arguably 让争论继续；undoubtedly 把争论结束。

abstract.en: Certainty is a door closed so quietly that nobody hears the argument outside.
abstract.cn: 确定是一扇关得很轻的门，轻到没人听见门外的争辩。

abstract.en: To say undoubtedly is to spend your last credit on one sentence.
abstract.cn: 说「毫无疑问」，就是把最后一点信用押在一句话上。

abstract.en: Doubt is not the opposite of knowledge but its shadow, which the word chooses to deny.
abstract.cn: 怀疑不是知识的反面，而是它的影子；这个词选择否认那道影子。

examples.en: The method is undoubtedly faster, though it costs more.
examples.cn: 这个方法无疑更快，尽管成本更高。

examples.en: Undoubtedly, some of the difference comes from the sample itself.
examples.cn: 毫无疑问，部分差异来自样本本身。

examples.en: He is undoubtedly the most experienced member of the team.
examples.cn: 他无疑是队里最有经验的成员。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「安道提德利」，doubt 是「怀疑」：把怀疑安放下去，就是毫无疑问地

root: 拉丁语 dubitare「犹豫、摇摆」← dubius「可疑的」（一般认为出自 duo「二」，心思被拉向两边）；古法语 doutier 丢掉 b 音，英语借入 doubt，十六世纪又按拉丁语补回不发音的 b。un- + doubted + -ly 构成副词。直接来源清楚；副词首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all remove doubt rather than reduce it: certainty that excludes reasonable doubt, a committed assertion, a fact beyond dispute, what is plain to see, a concession that buys the right to disagree, an insistence on the top of a scale, a publicly acknowledged standing, and a confident inference about what has already happened.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在取消怀疑，而不是减弱怀疑：排除合理怀疑的确定、作出承诺的断言、无可争议的事实、明摆着的实情、换取反驳权的让步、对刻度顶端的强调、公认的地位，以及对已发生之事的高确定推断。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people hesitating at a fork while a third walks straight through and does not look back.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个人在岔路口犹豫，第三个人径直走过，不再回头。

branches.en: DOUBT REMOVED: certainty that excludes reasonable doubt, and a finding no objection can touch.
branches.cn: 取消怀疑：排除合理怀疑的确定，以及任何反对都动不了的结论。

branches.en: THE COMMITMENT: the speaker stakes a full judgement on the sentence, and treats an inference about the past as settled.
branches.cn: 承诺：说话人把整个判断押在这句话上，并把对过去的推断当作已定。

branches.en: THE OBVIOUS: what any observer can see without argument.
branches.cn: 显然：任何观察者不必论证就看得见。

branches.en: THE CONCESSION: granting the opponent a certainty in order to disagree elsewhere.
branches.cn: 让步：把一份确定让给对手，好在别处提出异议。

branches.en: THE SUMMIT: insisting on the unique top of a scale, and a standing the whole field already accepts.
branches.cn: 顶点：坚持刻度上唯一的最高处，以及整个领域都已接受的声望。

intro.en: Undoubtedly is un- plus doubted plus -ly. Doubt is Latin dubitare through French, with b restored in spelling only. No further Latin entries are needed beyond the dubitare family.
intro.cn: undoubtedly 由 un-、doubted 与 -ly 构成。doubt 经法语来自拉丁语 dubitare，b 只在拼写上被补回。除 dubitare 词族外无需再列拉丁词条。

latinIntro.en: Dubius and dubitare supply the wavering image; un-, the English negative prefix, cancels it.
latinIntro.cn: dubius 与 dubitare 提供「摇摆」的意象；英语否定前缀 un- 把它取消。

items.example: The adjective describes a mind pulled between two readings.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述被两种读法拉扯的心思。

items.example: The verb supplies the act that un- later cancels.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供后来被 un- 取消的那个动作。

items.example: French drops the b in sound, and English follows French.
items.exampleCN: 法语在读音中丢掉 b，英语跟随法语。

items.example: The silent b marks the Latin origin, not the pronunciation.
items.exampleCN: 不发音的 b 标记拉丁来源，而不标记读音。

items.example: The participle lets un- negate a completed state.
items.exampleCN: 分词让 un- 能去否定一个已完成的状态。

items.example: The prefix removes the fork from the picture.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把岔路从画面里拿掉。

items.example: The adverb applies the certainty to a whole judgement.
items.exampleCN: 副词把这份确定加在整个判断上。

items.example: The -less form is a near synonym built on another suffix.
items.exampleCN: 带 -less 的形式是用另一个后缀构成的近义词。

items.example: Latin in- does the same work as English un-.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 in- 与英语 un- 起同样的作用。

items.example: It turns a doubted claim into an unquestioned one.
items.exampleCN: 它把被怀疑的说法变成不受质疑的说法。

definition_en: used to contrast two facts, or, in legal writing, to introduce the reasons for a document
core_image: 一条分水岭把坡面劈成两半，一边湿润一边干裂
scene: 北坡终年潮湿，石上长满青苔，南坡却干得裂开。The northern slope stays damp all year, whereas the southern side cracks in the sun.
sceneCN: 这里指把北坡与南坡两种情况对举（第 1 个义项：对比两个事实）；句意为北坡全年潮湿，而南坡在日晒下裂开。

pos.zh: 然而；而（对比两分句）；鉴于（法律文书开头）

derivatives.zh: 在哪里；在…的地方（构词成分）
借此；凭此（where + by 同构复合词）
为何；原因（where + fore 同构）

senses.title: Contrasting two clauses
senses.definition: used to join two statements and set one against the other
senses.definitionCN: 连接两个陈述，把其中一个与另一个对举
senses.example: The north is wet, whereas the south is dry.
senses.exampleCN: 北方湿润，而南方干燥。
senses.why: Where plus as originally meant at the same time that, so the word holds two facts side by side and lets the difference show.
senses.whyCN: where 加 as 原意为「在…的同时」，因此这个词把两件事实并排放着，让差异自己显出来。

senses.title: Contrasting figures
senses.definition: used in reports to set one set of numbers against another
senses.definitionCN: 报告中把一组数字与另一组对举
senses.example: Sales rose in spring, whereas they fell in autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 销售额春季上升，而秋季下降。
senses.why: Statistics need a neutral hinge between two curves, and the word supplies a contrast without claiming a cause.
senses.whyCN: 统计需要在两条曲线之间放一个中性的铰链，这个词提供对比而不主张原因。

senses.title: The reverse case
senses.definition: used to state the opposite case after describing one
senses.definitionCN: 描述一种情形之后陈述相反的另一种
senses.example: Some prefer speed, whereas others value accuracy.
senses.exampleCN: 有人看重速度，而另一些人看重准确。
senses.why: The second clause reverses the first, so the word functions as a mirror rather than a cause.
senses.whyCN: 第二句把第一句翻转过来，因此这个词起镜子的作用，而不是原因的作用。

senses.title: The legal recital: whereas
senses.definition: used at the start of a legal document to introduce the facts or reasons behind it
senses.definitionCN: 用于法律文件开头，引出文件所依据的事实或理由
senses.example: Whereas the parties have agreed to cooperate, this agreement is made.
senses.exampleCN: 鉴于各方已同意合作，特订立本协议。
senses.why: Legal drafting borrows the word for its oldest sense, seeing that, and turns it into a formal preamble marker.
senses.whyCN: 法律起草借用了这个词最古老的意义「既然、鉴于」，并把它变成正式的序言标记。

senses.title: Seeing that; since
senses.definition: formal: in view of the fact that; since
senses.definitionCN: 正式用语：鉴于…这一事实；既然
senses.example: Whereas the facts are established, we may proceed.
senses.exampleCN: 既然事实已经确立，我们可以继续。
senses.why: As supplies the causal reading, so the compound once meant because, and that older sense survives in statutes.
senses.whyCN: as 提供因果读法，因此这个复合词曾表「因为」，而这一较古的意义存留在法条里。

senses.title: Two qualities in one thing
senses.titleCN: 同一事物中的两种性质
senses.definition: used when two properties of a single thing are contrasted
senses.definitionCN: 对比同一事物的两种性质时使用
senses.example: The leaves are green, whereas the fruit is red.
senses.exampleCN: 叶子是绿的，而果实是红的。
senses.why: Contrast does not require two subjects: one object can hold two qualities, and the word still marks the difference.
senses.whyCN: 对比不必有两个主语：一个对象也可以带着两种性质，这个词照样标出差异。

senses.title: Claim against record
senses.definition: used to set a stated claim against what the evidence shows
senses.definitionCN: 把所声称的说法与证据所示对举
senses.example: He claims to be cautious, whereas his record shows recklessness.
senses.exampleCN: 他自称谨慎，而他的记录显示的却是鲁莽。
senses.why: When one clause is words and the other is facts, the contrast becomes an accusation without naming one.
senses.whyCN: 当一句是言辞、另一句是事实，对比就成了一种不必点名的指控。

senses.title: Formal comparison in academic prose
senses.titleCN: 学术写作中的正式对比
senses.definition: used in academic writing to compare two trends in one balanced sentence
senses.definitionCN: 学术写作中用一个平衡句比较两种趋势
senses.example: Urban incomes doubled, whereas rural wages stagnated.
senses.exampleCN: 城市收入翻倍，而农村工资停滞。
senses.why: Academic style prefers one long balanced sentence to two short ones, and this conjunction is the standard hinge for that balance.
senses.whyCN: 学术文体偏好一个长而平衡的句子而非两个短句，这个连词正是那种平衡的标准铰链。

intro.en: Whereas is an English compound of where and as, first recorded in the fourteenth century. It is Germanic, with no Latin cognate, so the Latin entries are left empty; the Latin cum and quamquam are counterparts only.
intro.cn: whereas 是 where 与 as 的英语复合词，最早见于十四世纪。它属日耳曼语，没有拉丁同族词，因此拉丁词条留空；拉丁语 cum 与 quamquam 只是对应词。

items.en: Hwær means where, the interrogative and relative place word that also gives where and wherever.
items.cn: hwær 意为「在哪里」，是疑问与关系处所词，也给出 where 与 wherever。

items.en: Eallswa, meaning wholly so, is the ancestor of as and supplies the second half of the compound.
items.cn: eallswa 意为「完全如此」，是 as 的祖先，提供复合词的后半截。

items.en: The parts join as wher-as with the sense at which time, and the word begins to carry contrast.
items.cn: 两部分合为 wher-as，义为「在…之时」，这个词开始带上对比义。

items.en: The form whereas is recorded in the fourteenth century, first as a relative adverb of time and place.
items.cn: whereas 这一形式记录于十四世纪，最初是表时间与处所的关系副词。

items.en: Legal drafting adopts whereas in the fifteenth century to open a document with its reasons, a use still standard in statutes and deeds.
items.cn: 法律起草在十五世纪采用 whereas 来以理由开篇，这一用法在法条与契据中至今仍是标准。

items.en: Modern English keeps the contrast sense and treats the legal recital as a separate, formal branch.
items.cn: 现代英语保留对比义，并把法律序言用法视为独立的正式分支。

note.en: The first group shares the where plus preposition pattern. The second group names contrast and concession, and separates whereas from although and while, which differ in what they concede.
note.cn: 第一组共享 where + 前置词的构词模式。第二组表示对比与让步，并把 whereas 与 although、while 分开，它们让步的内容不同。

entries.definition: In or at which place, the word the compound is built on.
entries.definitionCN: 在何处，复合词赖以构成的那个词。

entries.definition: By which means, with by in the second slot.
entries.definitionCN: 凭此、借此，第二格放 by。

entries.definition: In which, common in formal and legal writing.
entries.definitionCN: 在其中，常见于正式与法律文字。

entries.definition: After which, immediately following.
entries.definitionCN: 于是、随即，紧接其后。

entries.definition: In any place at all.
entries.definitionCN: 无论在什么地方。

entries.definition: Used to contrast two facts, often with a sense of simultaneous time.
entries.definitionCN: 用于对比两件事实，常带同时发生的意味。

entries.definition: The formal British variant of while in contrast.
entries.definitionCN: while 表对比时的英式正式变体。

entries.definition: Introduces a fact that works against the main clause; it concedes rather than balances.
entries.definitionCN: 引出与主句相抗的事实；它是让步而非对举。

entries.definition: The everyday contrastive conjunction, shorter and less formal.
entries.definitionCN: 日常转折连词，更短、更不正式。

entries.definition: Introducing the reverse of what was just said.
entries.definitionCN: 引出与刚说内容相反的情形。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real where plus as compound, the legal recital and the difference from although.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的 where + as 复合结构、法律序言用法，以及与 although 的区别。

normal.en: Where plus as once meant at the time that, so two facts simply stand side by side.
normal.cn: where 加 as 曾意为「在…之时」，于是两件事实就并排站着。

normal.en: Legal whereas is a preamble: the reasons come first, the operative words later.
normal.cn: 法律上的 whereas 是序言：理由在前，具体条款在后。

normal.en: Whereas balances two clauses; although concedes one and keeps the main clause standing.
normal.cn: whereas 让两个分句平衡；although 让步一句而让主句照旧成立。

normal.en: Whereas figures show: reports use the word so that two curves can be read in one line.
normal.cn: 「而数据显示」：报告用它，好把两条曲线放进一行里读。

normal.en: The word never gives a reason; it only shows a difference.
normal.cn: 这个词从不给理由，它只呈现差异。

abstract.en: A watershed does not judge either slope; it only draws the line between them.
abstract.cn: 分水岭不评判任何一面坡，它只画出两者之间的线。

abstract.en: Contrast is a way of letting two facts explain each other without a third sentence.
abstract.cn: 对比是一种让两件事实互相解释、而不需要第三句话的方式。

abstract.en: The quiet power of whereas is that it can accuse without naming anyone.
abstract.cn: whereas 的安静力量在于：它可以指控，却不点任何人的名。

examples.en: The old method was cheap, whereas the new one is fast.
examples.cn: 旧方法便宜，而新方法快。

examples.en: Whereas the first study used a small sample, the second surveyed a whole province.
examples.cn: 第一项研究样本很小，而第二项调查了整整一个省。

examples.en: He speaks of caution, whereas his actions show haste.
examples.cn: 他谈的是谨慎，而他的行动显出仓促。

root: 英语复合词 where（古英语 hwær「在哪里」）+ as（古英语 eallswa「完全如此」的缩略），十四世纪合为一词，初义「在…之时」，后固定为对比连词；十五世纪起用于法律文书开头的「鉴于」。属日耳曼语，无拉丁同族词，latinEntries 留空。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all set one thing against another: two clauses, two sets of figures, a reversed case, a legal preamble, the older sense of since, two qualities in one object, a claim against its record, and a balanced academic sentence.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在把一物与另一物对举：两个分句、两组数字、翻转的情形、法律序言、较古的「既然」义、同一对象的两种性质、说法与记录、学术写作中的平衡句。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a watershed splitting one slope into two, wet on one side and cracked on the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道分水岭把坡面劈成两半，一边湿润，一边干裂。

branches.en: TWO SIDES: two clauses side by side, and two qualities inside one object.
branches.cn: 两侧：两个分句并排，以及一个对象里的两种性质。

branches.en: THE MEASURED DIFFERENCE: two sets of figures, and the long balanced sentence of academic prose.
branches.cn: 有度量的差异：两组数字，以及学术文字中长而平衡的句子。

branches.en: THE MIRROR: the second clause stating the reverse of the first.
branches.cn: 镜像：第二句陈述第一句的反面。

branches.en: THE PREAMBLE: the legal recital, and the older sense of seeing that.
branches.cn: 序言：法律开篇的鉴于条款，以及较古的「既然」义。

branches.en: THE ACCUSATION: a stated claim set against what the record shows.
branches.cn: 指控：把声称的说法与记录所示对举。

intro.en: Whereas is a compound of where and as, not a prefixed word. English reuses where with prepositions in whereby, wherein and whereupon, and with -ever in wherever.
intro.cn: whereas 是 where 与 as 的复合词，不是加前缀的词。英语把 where 与前置词组合成 whereby、wherein、whereupon，并与 -ever 组合成 wherever。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic and has no Latin cognate, so no Latin entries are listed; cum and quamquam are only counterparts in meaning.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语，没有拉丁同族词，因此不列拉丁词条；cum 与 quamquam 仅在意义上对应。

items.structure: Old English hwær, interrogative and relative
items.example: The first half supplies the pointing to a place or a point in the text.
items.exampleCN: 前半截提供对某处或文中某一点的指向。

items.meaning: wholly so; in the manner that
items.example: The second half adds the sense of at the same time that.

items.example: The compound keeps both halves visible in meaning.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词的两个半截在意义上都还看得见。

items.example: The same frame defines a mechanism in contracts.
items.exampleCN: 同一框架在合同里用来界定某种机制。

items.example: Formal prose uses it to point inside a document.
items.exampleCN: 正式文字用它指向文件内部。

items.example: The word marks the next step in a legal narrative.
items.exampleCN: 这个词标出法律叙述中的下一步。

items.example: The -ever form generalises the place instead of contrasting it.
items.exampleCN: 带 -ever 的形式是把地点泛化，而不是对举。

items.example: The formal British variant competes with whereas in contrast.
items.exampleCN: 这个英式正式变体在对比用法上与 whereas 竞争。

items.structure: Old English hwīl, noun used as conjunction
items.example: The everyday alternative adds a hint of simultaneous time.
items.exampleCN: 这个日常替代词多带一点「同时」的意味。

items.meaning: in spite of the fact that
items.example: The concessive neighbour concedes instead of balancing.
items.exampleCN: 这个让步的邻居是让步，而不是对举。

definition_en: by which; used to introduce the means or mechanism by which something is done
core_image: 一根绳子系在两岸，人正是抓着它过河
scene: 村里定下一条规矩：每户每年出一个人去修渠。The village agreed on a rule whereby each household sends one worker to repair the channel each year.
sceneCN: 这里指这条规矩所规定的机制（第 1 个义项：凭此、借此引出实现方式）；句意为村里定下一条规矩，凭它每户每年派一人修渠。

pos.zh: 凭此；借此；通过…方式（关系副词，相当于「凭这个」）

derivatives.zh: 在哪里；在…之处（构词成分）
借此；由此（there + by 的同构复合词）
然而；鉴于（where + as 同构）

senses.title: The mechanism in a rule
senses.definition: used to introduce the mechanism that a rule or system sets up
senses.definitionCN: 引出某条规则或制度所设立的运作机制
senses.example: They agreed on a system whereby each member reports twice a year.
senses.exampleCN: 他们商定了一种制度，凭它每位成员每年报告两次。
senses.why: Where points at the arrangement and by names the means, so the compound asks the reader to look inside the thing just mentioned for its workings.
senses.whyCN: where 指向那个安排，by 指出手段，因此这个复合词让读者到刚提到的事物内部去看它如何运转。

senses.title: The method in a process
senses.definition: used to name the method by which a process is carried out
senses.definitionCN: 引出完成某一过程所采用的方法
senses.example: They describe a process whereby waste is turned into fuel.
senses.exampleCN: 他们描述了一种过程，借此把废弃物变成燃料。
senses.why: The relative adverb attaches the method to the noun it follows, so the method is presented as belonging to the process itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个关系副词把方法挂在前面的名词上，因此方法被呈现为过程自身的一部分。

senses.title: The formula in a contract
senses.titleCN: 合同条款里的计算公式
senses.definition: used in legal drafting to introduce a formula or condition
senses.definitionCN: 法律起草中引出某一计算公式或条件
senses.example: The clause sets a formula whereby rent rises with inflation.
senses.exampleCN: 该条款订出一个公式，据此租金随通胀上调。
senses.why: Contracts must tie an obligation to a precise route, and whereby is the standard hinge for that route.
senses.whyCN: 合同必须把义务拴在一条精确的路线上，而 whereby 就是那条路线的标准铰链。

senses.title: The means to a result
senses.definition: used to show the means by which a result is produced
senses.definitionCN: 表明产生某一结果所凭的手段
senses.example: The valve opens, whereby pressure is released.
senses.exampleCN: 阀门打开，压力借此释放。
senses.why: Here the means and the result touch: opening the valve is the route by which the release happens.
senses.whyCN: 这里手段与结果相接：打开阀门正是压力得以释放的那条路。

senses.title: The channel for delivery
senses.titleCN: 资金或信息传递的渠道
senses.definition: used of a channel through which something reaches its destination
senses.definitionCN: 指某物抵达目的地所经的渠道
senses.example: They set up an arrangement whereby funds reach the villages directly.
senses.exampleCN: 他们做出一种安排，凭此资金直接到达各村。
senses.why: A channel is a by-route in space, which is why the compound suits money, goods and information.
senses.whyCN: 渠道是空间中的「经由之路」，所以这个复合词适用于资金、货物与信息。

senses.title: The tool for a task
senses.definition: used to name an instrument that makes a task possible
senses.definitionCN: 引出使某项任务得以完成的工具
senses.example: They designed a tool whereby the parts can be checked in seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 他们设计了一种工具，借它几秒钟就能检查这些零件。
senses.why: An instrument is the most concrete kind of by, so the word naturally introduces devices as well as procedures.
senses.whyCN: 工具是「凭借」最具体的一种，因此这个词既能引出程序，也能引出器具。

senses.title: The relation between quantities
senses.definition: used in definitions to state the relation by which one quantity depends on another
senses.definitionCN: 在定义中陈述一个量依赖另一个量所凭的关系
senses.example: It is a relation whereby one quantity depends on another.
senses.exampleCN: 这是一种关系，凭它一个量取决于另一个量。
senses.why: Mathematics defines by relations, and the compound names the link that makes the definition work.
senses.whyCN: 数学靠关系作定义，这个复合词命名了使定义成立的那条联系。

senses.title: The act that creates a legal status
senses.definition: used in legal narrative for an act by which a status or liability arises
senses.definitionCN: 法律叙述中指产生某种地位或责任的举动
senses.example: He signed the deed, whereby he became responsible for the debt.
senses.exampleCN: 他签署了这份契据，据此他对该债务负责。
senses.why: In law an act can create an obligation, and the word marks the exact step where the status changes.
senses.whyCN: 在法律上，一个行为可以产生一项义务，这个词标出地位改变的那一步。

intro.en: Whereby is an English compound of where and by, first recorded in the thirteenth century. It is Germanic and has no Latin cognate, so no Latin entries are listed; the Latin qua and per quae are counterparts only.
intro.cn: whereby 是 where 与 by 的英语复合词，最早见于十三世纪。它属日耳曼语，没有拉丁同族词，因此不列拉丁词条；拉丁语 qua 与 per quae 只是对应说法。

items.en: Hwær is the place word behind where, used both to ask and to relate.
items.cn: hwær 是 where 背后的处所词，既用于提问也用于关联。

items.en: Bi means near or by means of, and English by keeps both the place sense and the instrumental one.
items.cn: bi 意为在近旁、凭借，英语 by 既保留处所义，也保留工具义。

items.en: Wher-bi appears in early Middle English with the sense by which, tying a means to the noun before it.
items.cn: wher-bi 见于中古英语早期，义为「凭此」，把手段拴在前面的名词上。

items.en: Drafters of statutes and contracts adopt the word because it can pin an obligation to an exact route.
items.cn: 法条与合同的起草者采用这个词，因为它能把义务钉在一条精确的路线上。

items.en: Modern English keeps whereby mostly in formal, legal and technical prose; ordinary speech prefers by which or where.
items.cn: 现代英语主要在正式、法律与技术文字中保留 whereby；日常口语更爱用 by which 或 where。

note.en: The first group shares the where plus preposition pattern. The second group names the by-route in plainer words, which modern speech prefers.
note.cn: 第一组共享 where + 前置词的构词模式。第二组用更朴素的词说出「经由之路」，现代口语更偏爱它们。

entries.definition: In or at which place; the word the compound is built on.
entries.definitionCN: 在何处；复合词赖以构成的那个词。

entries.definition: By that means, pointing back instead of setting up a relative clause.
entries.definitionCN: 借此、由此，回指前文，而不是引导关系从句。

entries.definition: In which, pointing inside an arrangement rather than to its means.
entries.definitionCN: 在其中，指向安排内部，而非指向手段。

entries.definition: After which, immediately following an event.
entries.definitionCN: 于是、随即，紧接某事件之后。

entries.definition: In contrast, or in legal recitals, seeing that.
entries.definitionCN: 然而；在法律序言中作「鉴于」。

entries.definition: The plain relative phrase that whereby replaces.
entries.definitionCN: whereby 所替代的朴素关系短语。

entries.definition: Naming a channel rather than a tool.
entries.definitionCN: 指渠道而非工具。

entries.definition: An explicit statement of instrumentality.
entries.definitionCN: 明确说出「凭借手段」。

entries.definition: Used of a rule or arrangement rather than a method.
entries.definitionCN: 用于规则或安排，而非方法。

entries.definition: Introduces a purpose or result rather than a mechanism.
entries.definitionCN: 引出目的或结果，而不是机制。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real where plus by compound, the contract formula and the plain phrase by which.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的 where + by 复合结构、合同公式，以及朴素说法 by which。

normal.en: Where plus by is literally at which by, the junction of a place and a means.
normal.cn: where 加 by 字面上是「在那一处凭借」，是地点与手段的接合处。

normal.en: Contracts love whereby because an obligation needs a route, not a slogan.
normal.cn: 合同喜欢 whereby，因为义务需要的是一条路线，而不是一句口号。

normal.en: In every day speech people say by which; whereby belongs to the written register.
normal.cn: 日常说话人们用 by which；whereby 属于书面语域。

normal.en: Thereby points back, whereby points forward to the mechanism that follows.
normal.cn: thereby 回指前文，whereby 则指向后面要说明的机制。

normal.en: A valve opening whereby pressure escapes is mechanism and result in one breath.
normal.cn: 「阀门打开，压力借此释放」一口气说出了机制与结果。

abstract.en: A rope across a river is not the crossing, but it is the whereby of the crossing.
abstract.cn: 横在河上的绳子不是渡河本身，但它是渡河的「凭此」。

abstract.en: Every institution is a whereby written down and forgotten.
abstract.cn: 每一项制度都是被写下来、然后被遗忘的「凭此」。

abstract.en: The word asks one question only: through what does this happen?
abstract.cn: 这个词只问一个问题：这件事经由什么发生？

examples.en: They created a channel whereby complaints reach the manager directly.
examples.cn: 他们建立了一条渠道，凭此投诉能直达经理。

examples.en: The treaty established a procedure whereby disputes are settled by arbitration.
examples.cn: 该条约确立了一套程序，据此争端通过仲裁解决。

examples.en: There is no known mechanism whereby the signal could cross the barrier.
examples.cn: 目前没有已知的机制能让该信号越过这道屏障。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「威尔拜」，where 是「那里」，by 是「凭借」：在那里凭借它，就是凭此

root: 英语复合词 where（古英语 hwær「在哪里」）+ by（古英语 bī「在旁、凭借」），十三世纪合为一词，义为「凭此」，作关系副词把手段拴在其前的名词上。属日耳曼语，无拉丁同族词，latinEntries 留空。现代英语主要保留于法律、合同与技术文字。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all answer through what: the mechanism of a rule, the method of a process, the formula in a contract, the route to a result, the channel of delivery, the tool for a task, the relation between quantities, and the act that creates a legal status.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在回答「经由什么」：规则的机制、过程的方法、合同里的公式、通往结果的路、传递的渠道、任务的工具、量之间的关系，以及产生法律地位的举动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rope stretched across a river, the thing people actually hold on to.
core.cn: 核心意象：横跨河面的一根绳子，正是人实际抓住的东西。

branches.en: THE RULE: the working mechanism built into a system.
branches.cn: 规则：制度内部自带的运作机制。

branches.en: THE METHOD AND TOOL: how a process runs, and the instrument that makes a task possible.
branches.cn: 方法与工具：过程如何运转，以及使任务可行的器具。

branches.en: THE FORMULA: the precise route a clause writes into an obligation.
branches.cn: 公式：条款写进义务的那条精确路线。

branches.en: THE WAY THROUGH: the means that produces a result, and the channel that delivers it.
branches.cn: 经由之路：产生结果的手段，以及把结果送达的渠道。

branches.en: THE LINK AND THE ACT: a relation between quantities, and a step that changes a legal status.
branches.cn: 联系与举动：量之间的关系，以及改变法律地位的一步。

intro.en: Whereby is a compound of where and by rather than a prefixed word. English reuses where with prepositions in wherein, whereupon and whereas, and with there in thereby.
intro.cn: whereby 是 where 与 by 的复合词，不是加前缀的词。英语把 where 与前置词组成 wherein、whereupon、whereas，并与 there 组成 thereby。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic and has no Latin cognate, so no Latin entries are listed; qua and per quae express the same link in Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语，没有拉丁同族词，因此不列拉丁词条；拉丁语 qua 与 per quae 表达同一种联系。

items.exampleCN: 第一个成分指向正在描述的那个安排。

items.example: The second element supplies instrumentality.

items.example: The same frame can name a location inside a document.

items.example: The frame also carries sequence in legal narrative.

items.example: The contrastive cousin takes as instead of by.

items.example: It is the plain phrase that the compound compresses.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个复合词所压缩的朴素短语。

items.example: The noun names what the by element contributes.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词说出 by 成分所贡献的内容。

items.example: Technical prose often prefers this noun to the compound.

definition_en: although; used to add a fact that limits what has just been said, usually before a short phrase
core_image: 一扇门开了一条缝，人能进去，但只能侧着身
scene: 新水泵装好了，声音有点吵，但出水量确实大了。The new pump works well, albeit noisily.
